If the directory piles up thousands of files, they are processed without losing data. The XML files are moved to a temporary directory and returned in batches:

mkdir -p /tmp/xml
mv /var/spool/pandora/data_in/*data /tmp/xml
ls -rt /tmp/xml | grep data | head -20 | xargs -i% mv /tmp/xml/% /var/spool/pandora/data_in

The last command returns 20 each time: it is repeated until the temporary directory is empty, letting the server process them between one batch and the next. Do not delete the XML files if they can contain data you need to recover.

docs.title: Deleting an agent from a satellite server
docs.text:
An agent created by a satellite server does not disappear by deleting it only in the console: the satellite creates it again. It has to be removed at the source:

  1. Delete it from the hosts file of the satellite (by default /etc/pandora/satellite_hosts.txt, or the one its configuration indicates in host_file).
  2. Delete the configuration file of that agent in the directory of the satellite (by default /etc/pandora/conf, or the one it has configured in agent_conf_dir).

After that, in the console, delete the agent.

docs.title: Uploading larger files from the console
docs.text:
When the console rejects a file (for example, when adding it to a collection), there are two limits to raise:

  • PHP: the upload_max_filesize value (and post_max_size) in php.ini, and restart the web service.
  • The console: the Collection size (Bytes) setting in Management → Settings → System Settings → General setup (token collection_max_size). It comes with one million bytes by default.

If only one is changed, the other one keeps cutting.

docs.title: Server and database
docs.text:
The two pieces everything else depends on: the server that processes and the database that stores. When one fails, the other notices.

The Pandora FMS server is an application with several internal servers. When it does not start, restarts on its own or goes down, the log says why. Almost everything is solved by reading it before touching anything.

docs.title: The server does not start
docs.text:
The first thing is the two log files:

  • /var/log/pandora/pandora_server.log
  • /var/log/pandora/pandora_server.error

The specific error shows up there. Also check MySQL, which is indeed a dependency of the server. tentacle_serverd is a separate service: if it is stopped, the EndPoints will not be able to deliver data over Tentacle, but that alone does not prevent pandora_server from starting.

docs.title: The server restarts in a loop
docs.text:
When something kills it and brings it back up every few minutes, the suspect is the start-up time. The server_keepalive token in /etc/pandora/pandora_server.conf is 45 seconds by default. If the server takes longer than that to become operational, the high availability system does not see it as active and restarts it, and so on in a loop.

The usual cause is having raised the threads of the internal servers (*_threads): the more threads, the longer it takes to start. It is fixed by raising server_keepalive so that it covers that start-up.

docs.title: The server goes down
docs.text:
The same log is checked and, if nothing appears, these causes are ruled out in order:

  • Not enough memory. The server runs out of RAM and the system kills it.
  • MySQL. A database that runs slow or goes down drags the server with it.
  • Full nodes. In a Command Center, a node with no space stops responding.
  • A half-finished update. Wrong packages or a database schema update that did not finish.

docs.title: "Segmentation fault" when starting the server
docs.text: It may appear when more threads have been assigned than the hardware can initialize and sustain. Check the *_threads tokens in the file and reduce the ones that were raised without a measurement to justify it. There is no fixed equivalence between threads and modules: it depends on the check type, the interval, the concurrency and the hardware. Measure before raising them again.

docs.title: Enabling or stopping internal servers
docs.text:
Each internal server is turned on and off with its token in /etc/pandora/pandora_server.conf: 1 enables it and 0 disables it. The ones needed according to the use case are explained in Introduction and architecture.

After changing the file, the service must be restarted:

systemctl restart pandora_server

A stopped internal server gives no error: it simply does not do its job, so if something "is not processed" and the token is set to 0, you already know where to look.

docs.title: Running the database purge by hand
docs.text:
Maintenance is installed in /etc/cron.hourly/pandora_db and calls the tool with the server configuration:

/usr/share/pandora_server/util/pandora_db.pl /etc/pandora/pandora_server.conf

Old Enterprise installations also had an executable in /usr/bin/pandora_db; today the right path is the one in util/.

If it has never been run, the first pass can take hours: launch it in the background and do not cut it short.

docs.title: The kernel warns of "possible SYN flooding on port 41121"
docs.text:
The Tentacle port is 41121/TCP. A high count of TIME_WAIT connections can be a clue, but it does not on its own prove that the SYN queue is saturated. Also look at the SYN_RECV connections and the retransmission counters before changing kernel parameters:

netstat -an | grep TIME_WAIT | wc -l

Some current deployments set tcp_max_syn_backlog to 65536. It is not a universal value and does not on its own fix a network or capacity problem: first identify where connections are being dropped.

net.ipv4.tcp_max_syn_backlog = 65536

Do not use tcp_tw_recycle

The net.ipv4.tcp_tw_recycle parameter that old guides recommended was removed from the Linux kernel in version 4.12. Do not look for it and do not add it.

In the database, the usual causes are maintenance that is not run, a damaged table, slow storage or a badly sized data retention.

docs.title: How to back up the database
docs.text:
The product brings its own tool: pandora_backup.sh, in /usr/share/pandora_server/util/. The console path is passed with -c; the backup destination, with -d:

# Backup (database + console files)
/usr/share/pandora_server/util/pandora_backup.sh \
    -c /var/www/html/pandora_console -d /tmp

# Restore the database from a backup
/usr/share/pandora_server/util/pandora_backup.sh \
    -c /var/www/html/pandora_console \
    -s /path/to/the/backup/pandorafms_backup_date.tar.gz

# Restore files and configuration too (in addition to the database)
/usr/share/pandora_server/util/pandora_backup.sh \
    -c /var/www/html/pandora_console \
    -s /path/to/the/backup/pandorafms_backup_date.tar.gz -f

The console path passed with -c is also necessary when restoring: the tool uses it to read the database credentials. Without -f, it restores the database, but not the console files or the configuration. With -f it also restores those files and the spool; -b excludes the database. Restoring the database deletes and recreates the configured database. Check the file and make a copy of the current state before continuing.

If you prefer to do it by hand, the database and the user are usually called pandora. The restore example assumes the database already exists:

mysqldump -u pandora -p pandora > /path/pandora_backup_date.sql
mysql -u pandora -p pandora < /path/pandora_backup_date.sql

Credentials are checked in /etc/pandora/pandora_server.conf, in the dbuser, dbpass and dbname fields. They are not copied here.

docs.title: The database runs slow
docs.text:
Before touching the MySQL configuration, rule out these four causes, in order:

  1. Maintenance is not running. The package leaves the script in /etc/cron.hourly/pandora_db, which calls /usr/share/pandora_server/util/pandora_db.pl with the server configuration. If it has been lost or cron does not run, the database grows without limit. Run it by hand and see if it reports an error.
  2. The retention does not match the use. Review the purge periods and, in large environments, whether old data should be moved to a historical database. There is no universal period: it depends on how much data is collected and how much needs to be queried.
  3. Storage. Check latency, free space and read and write load. A saturated disk affects both MySQL and the server.
  4. MySQL fine tuning. Parameters such as innodb_buffer_pool_size or innodb_io_capacity are tuned to the real size of the machine and the data volume. There are no universal values: you start from a recommendation for the server size and measure.

docs.title: The console warns of "Database maintenance"
docs.text:
That warning means that maintenance is not running. The database needs that script every hour: it purges old data, compacts and moves to the historical database whatever corresponds.

Check that it exists and works:

/usr/share/pandora_server/util/pandora_db.pl /etc/pandora/pandora_server.conf

If the script answers that "another instance seems to be running", the MySQL named lock indicates that another connection is running maintenance. The lock is released when it finishes or the connection closes. Check whether there is another active run and review its logs; do not delete by hand a supposed lock indicator in the configuration table.

docs.title: Database error when starting the server
docs.text:
If the server log shows a connection failure on start-up (DBI connect ... failed), check these two points first:

  • The password or the user are not correct. Test by hand with mysql -u pandora -p -h 127.0.0.1 -D pandora and compare them with the dbuser, dbpass and dbname fields of /etc/pandora/pandora_server.conf.
  • The configured host is localhost and the socket does not match. Some MySQL packages use /var/lib/mysql/mysql.sock instead of /tmp/mysql.sock. The current default value of dbhost is 127.0.0.1, which uses TCP; if your installation uses localhost, check the real path of the socket first before changing it.

In current versions dbhost comes with 127.0.0.1, which avoids localhost resolution problems over IPv6.

docs.title: The database does not respond and there is too much data
docs.text: There is no universal number of records from which the database stops responding. The data volume, the write rate, the queries, the retention and the hardware all play a part. Before rebuilding anything, review the MySQL log, the space and the load; confirm that maintenance works and that the purge and historical policy matches what you need. Make a copy before any repair. A rebuild or restore of the database must be planned with a DBA: do not delete the data directory or the database blindly.

docs.title: "Table is marked as crashed and should be repaired"
docs.text:
REPAIR TABLE is only useful for engines that support that operation, such as MyISAM. The main Pandora FMS tables use InnoDB: check the engine and the specific error first before attempting a repair:

SHOW TABLE STATUS LIKE 'table_name';

If the table uses MyISAM, REPAIR TABLE table_name; may be appropriate. If it uses InnoDB, that is not the procedure: keep the error log and check the engine diagnostics or restore a validated copy with a DBA.

docs.title: Corruption in the database
docs.text: Before attempting a repair, identify the engine of the table. mysqlcheck --auto-repair is only useful for engines that support that operation, such as MyISAM; it does not repair InnoDB. The main Pandora FMS tables use InnoDB. Keep the error log, make a copy and check the recovery procedure for that engine with a DBA. Do not delete /var/lib/mysql or recreate the database as a first attempt.

docs.title: "PROCESS privilege" error when making a dump
docs.text:
In MySQL 8, if mysqldump fails for lack of the PROCESS privilege when reading tablespaces, first try to skip them with --no-tablespaces:

mysqldump --no-tablespaces -u pandora -p pandora > /path/backup.sql

That way there is no need to grant PROCESS globally to the application user just to make a copy. If your version does not accept the option, check with the DBA before changing the privileges.

docs.title: Maintenance also processes the historical database
docs.text: The standard hourly maintenance manages the historical database when it is configured. The server reads the connection parameters saved in the main database configuration and connects with the host, the database and the user indicated there. There is no need to create another cron task with a manual copy of pandora_server.conf. Check that the historical database is enabled and that the configured connection works.

docs.title: Agents and systems
docs.text: The EndPoint collects data from the machine. This section covers start-up, the XML queues and the monitoring specific to Windows and Linux: PowerShell, services and logs.

docs.title: The new EndPoint does not show up in the Web console
docs.text:
Check these in order:

  1. The agent points to the right server. In pandora_agent.conf, the server_ip token carries the Pandora FMS server address and server_port the Tentacle port, which is 41121. If the port is not that one, the agent writes into the void.
  2. The server accepts new agents. In /etc/pandora/pandora_server.conf, the autocreate 1 token makes the agents that arrive without a previous registration create themselves, in the group set by autocreate_group. With autocreate at 0 and an agent that does not declare a group, its data is discarded without further notice.
  3. The network. The EndPoint is the one that starts the connection to the server, so the firewall has to let 41121/TCP through from the machine to the server.

docs.title: Testing Tentacle from the command line
docs.text:
The client starts the connection to the Tentacle server, by default on port 41121/TCP. For a test, send a valid data file from the agent machine:

tentacle_client -a 192.0.2.10 -v /path/to/the/agent.data

Replace the IP and the path with those of your environment. Run the test on a test machine or with a real data XML: the server receives the file and processes it. If it fails, check that tentacle_serverd is active, that it listens on the expected port and that the firewall allows the traffic. The password, certificate, alternative port and proxy options are in the Tentacle reference.

docs.title: The EndPoint service does not start on Windows
docs.text:
Check two things before touching anything:

  • It was installed without administrator permissions. The installer has to run as administrator and the service needs SYSTEM permissions. If not, it does not start.
  • There is a stray PandoraAgent.exe in the installer folder. If the installer finds an executable in its own path, the service points to that one and not to the one in the agent folder, so it fails at start-up. Before installing, leave the folder clean.

To tell a service problem from an EndPoint problem, run the start-up script in the scripts folder with Run as administrator. If it starts that way, check the account configured in the service properties.

docs.title: The XML files pile up in data_in
docs.text:
The files that EndPoints leave in /var/spool/pandora/data_in pile up when processing cannot keep up. The checking order is:

  1. The server is running. With the server stopped, the queue grows and that is it. Check it with systemctl status pandora_server.
  2. How many BADXML files there are. They are files the server has not been able to read: 
    ls /var/spool/pandora/data_in | grep -c BADXML
    If there are many, they are cleaned up and the cause is looked for (next section).
  3. The Data server threads. The dataserver_threads token in /etc/pandora/pandora_server.conf is 1 by default. On a server with many machines, raising it speeds up the emptying of the queue.

docs.title: There are BADXML files
docs.text:
A BADXML is an XML the server has not been able to parse, almost always because a module has put in a value that breaks the file. The error is located without guessing:

xmllint TempTHXDF01.211810.data_BADXML

The command points to the exact line. With that, go to the XML, see which module generates that content and correct the module so that it returns a valid data item. The BADXML files already generated can be deleted: the agent will send them again, corrected, in the next interval.

docs.title: A lot of data arrived at once and the server is running behind
docs.text: After a server outage, the EndPoints have kept collecting data and the queue fills up at once. The server has a processing mode designed for that: the dataserver_smart_queue token, which already comes enabled in current versions (1). If the installation is old and it is at 0, set it to 1. And if the volume is high, raise the dataserver_threads.

docs.title: The data arrives duplicated
docs.text:
It is not that the server duplicates it: there is something repeated at the source. Check in this order:

  • Two agents with the same name. It is the most common case. To locate them, temporarily add to that agent a module that returns the machine IP (ipconfig on Windows, ip address on Linux) and see how many IPs answer with the same name.
  • Two modules with the same name inside the agent, or a module and a plugin that obtain the same data.
  • A module that returns more than one value. Run it by hand on the machine and check that its output is a single data item.

docs.title: The agent inventory does not arrive
docs.text: Since version 784 there is no inventory server of its own: that task was absorbed by the Heavy Server, which comes active by default (heavyserver 1). If the inventory does not show up, check that the EndPoint has its inventory plugin enabled and that the Heavy Server is running. The old inventoryserver token no longer exists.

docs.title: Configuring the EndPoint from the console
docs.text: It can be done if the agent allows it: the remote_config token in pandora_agent.conf is 1 by default, so the agent accepts its configuration being changed from the Web console. If someone set it to 0, from then on it stops accepting remote changes and the file has to be edited by hand.

docs.title: Characters better avoided in agent and module names
docs.text: So that the internal paths and commands do not get confused, it is better to avoid /, \, |, %, #, & and $ in the name of an agent or a module. They are characters the system interprets in paths and executions, and having problems with them is a matter of time.

docs.title: Basic Windows monitoring
docs.text:
Once the EndPoint is installed, the quickest way is not to write modules by hand:

  • Apply one of the policies the console brings for Windows machines, which already includes the basic set of checks.
  • Or use the module templates in the agent configuration, in the Module templates section.

When the policy or the template is applied, the modules are written into the agent configuration file. They start reporting in the next interval. For specifics of your environment, own modules (or scripts and plugins) are added on top of that base.

docs.title: Basic Linux monitoring
docs.text: It is the same path: policies per operating system that the console brings, or module templates from the agent configuration. With that they already report CPU, memory, disk, processes and the usual services; the specific part is added by hand or with a plugin.

docs.title: Running a PowerShell script in a module
docs.text:
The Windows EndPoint knows how to run PowerShell. It is given the path of the executable and the script:

module_begin
module_name Module_name
module_type generic_data
module_exec C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe -Command "C:\Path\script.ps1"
module_end

The module type is chosen according to what the script returns:

Type What it is for generic_data A numeric data item generic_data_string An alphanumeric data item generic_proc A boolean value (1 or 0)

If the script returns text, generic_data is not valid: the module will show up as Unknown.

docs.title: Starting or stopping a service or a process
docs.text:
There are two mechanisms, and it is better not to confuse them:

  • Postconditions: the module, besides measuring, runs something when a condition on its value is met. module_condition carries an operator, a value and the response command. The syntax and the operators are detailed in the EndPoint reference.
  • Windows watchdog: module_proc can relaunch a crashed process with module_watchdog and module_start_command. module_service watches a Windows service and restarts it directly. It is also explained in the EndPoint reference.

docs.title: Monitoring Windows logs
docs.text:
The Windows EndPoint brings three ways:

  • Logevent: reads the Windows system events; the category of interest is chosen.
  • Regexp: looks for a pattern inside a specific log file.
  • Log plugins: the same search, with a script, useful when the format is custom.

docs.title: Monitoring Linux logs
docs.text:
The two plugins used are:

  • grep_log: given a path, it looks for the content you indicate and creates the module with the result.
  • grep_log_module: the same, but it also sends the log to the Pandora FMS log collector with Syslog as source, so that it stays in the viewer.

The practical difference: the first one measures, the second one also archives.

docs.title: User variables when the EndPoint does not run as root
docs.text:
If the EndPoint runs with a user other than root, the modules that depend on that user's environment can fail. Check:

  1. That the user's home exists.
  2. That it has a valid shell (for example, /bin/bash); for security, it comes disabled.
  3. That the environment variables it needs are in its $HOME/.bashrc (that file does not exist by default: it has to be created).
  4. That the file is readable and that the whole home belongs to that user.

With the four things in order, the EndPoint inherits the environment on start-up.

docs.title: Web console and licences
docs.text:
Getting into the console and keeping it in shape: access, security settings and the licence that enables the platform.

The Web console is the gateway to the platform. Here the access, display, security and licence problems are gathered.

docs.title: I have lost the administrator password
docs.text:
The console does not bring a "forgot password" by email for the administrator, so it is solved from the server, with the management tool:

/usr/share/pandora_server/util/pandora_manage.pl /etc/pandora/pandora_server.conf \
    --create_user temporary_admin CHANGE_THIS_PASSWORD 1

That creates a temporary administrator user. Log in with it, change the password of the original user and delete the temporary user, so as not to leave an open door.

Do not leave the temporary user

The original entry proposed creating it with the password none. Do not do it: set a real password and delete the account as soon as you finish.

docs.title: Changing a user's password from the command line
docs.text:
With the same pandora_manage.pl, without creating new accounts:

/usr/share/pandora_server/util/pandora_manage.pl /etc/pandora/pandora_server.conf \
    --update_user USER_ID password NEW_PASSWORD

The command also works for other user fields: email, phone, language, theme (id_skin), full name and whether the user is an administrator.

docs.title: The console shows up blank or with MySQL errors
docs.text:
Two causes, in order of frequency:

  • A half-finished update or installation. Some console file was left corrupt. The console packages are reinstalled in the same version that was already installed.
  • Schema MRs are missing. If there are also MySQL errors, the most likely thing is that the database was left at a previous MR. The missing ones are applied.

If that does not fix it, the console is reinstalled from scratch keeping include/config.php, the content of attachment and the custom images.

docs.title: I cannot get in and the disk is full
docs.text:
When the disk fills up, MySQL cannot write, the console does not open and the new data stops being processed. What has eaten it up is looked for:

  • Backups that pile up and nobody deletes. It is the first thing to look at.
  • Logs that are not being purged.
  • Files with an anomalous size. They are moved or deleted, carefully.
  • The database. Text modules (generic_data_string) are the ones that grow the most: they store long strings that repeat on every interval.

docs.title: The graphs do not show text
docs.text:
If the graph comes out without axes or values, the font with which the text is drawn is missing. The path is declared in the console configuration, in the fontpath setting. It has to be checked that the font exists at that path and that the web server user can read it.

Notice

The old entries talked about the $config_homedir variable. That setting no longer exists: if no texts appear on the graphs, look at fontpath.

docs.title: The console responds slowly
docs.text:
There are two places to look at, and they are told apart with the log and with the consumption:

  1. The web server. If the Apache processes consume 100% of CPU or memory, the problem is there: resources are missing, or php.ini falls short of memory (memory_limit). PHP limit errors appear in the Apache log or in pandora_console.log.
  2. MySQL. If the web server has room to spare and the console is still slow, the bottleneck is in the database. See Server and database.

docs.title: I lost the two-factor authentication code generator
docs.text:
Two-factor authentication (2FA) is disabled for a user from the server:

/usr/share/pandora_server/util/pandora_manage.pl /etc/pandora/pandora_server.conf \
    --disable_double_auth '<user>'

It works both if you are the one who has lost the generator and if you are the administrator and someone else asks you. If what you want is to turn it off for the whole console, there is the double_auth_enabled setting in the tconfig table, but for a single account the command is cleaner.

docs.title: Console themes and a copy of the styles
docs.text: Themes are changed from the Web console, in the user preferences. Before touching icons or custom styles it is better to make a copy: the product brings styles_backup.sh in the server utilities folder (pandora_server/util/), which exports the icons and the CSS to pandora_console/styles_backup in two compressed files with date and time.

docs.title: Putting the console on HTTPS
docs.text:
The console is served over HTTPS with a web server certificate:

  1. Have the certificate and its key ready (.crt and .key). Do not use self-signed ones: they are not trustworthy for the user and they do not avoid the warnings.
  2. Configure Apache to listen on 443 and point to those files (SSLCertificateFile and SSLCertificateKeyFile).
  3. Restart the web service.
  4. If you want nobody to get in over HTTP, enable the setting that forces the use of HTTPS in Management → Settings → System Settings → General setup.

docs.title: AD or LDAP authentication does not work
docs.text:
Pandora FMS supports both, and they share almost all the configuration. If the users cannot get in, check:

  • Server and port of the LDAP or of the domain.
  • The search function: Local Command uses the ldapsearch command (it has to be installed on the Pandora FMS server); PHP function uses the console's own engine. The normal thing is PHP function, and Local Command only makes sense in very large environments.
  • The base domain and the organisational units / groups: this is where everybody gets it wrong. The search path has to point exactly to where the users are.

docs.title: Console time zone
docs.text:
The console uses the system zone; if it is not defined, it falls back to the European one. If the data shows up with another time, set the time zone in Management → Settings → System Settings → General setup (timezone setting).

The old entries proposed editing include/config_process.php and forcing date_default_timezone_set. It still works, but it is plan B: better to leave it consistent with the operating system.

docs.title: Notifications: managing and deleting them
docs.text:
• Deleting them: from Workspace → Messages → Message list, where they can all be deleted.
  • Configuring them: in Management → Settings → System Settings → Notifications they are activated or deactivated per type and assigned to users or groups. Each user also has their own configuration of what they want to receive.

docs.title: Where PHP failures show up
docs.text:
There are two places, and it is better to look at both:

  • The web server log: error_log, or ssl_error_log if the console runs over HTTPS. Check in /etc/php.ini that error logging is active and that the path is defined.
  • The console's own log: it has to be enabled in Management → Settings → System Settings → General setup → Enable console log, and it is written to pandora_console/log/console.log.

To debug temporarily, the PHP reporting can be raised from the console's include/config.php:

error_reporting(E_ALL);

When you finish, bring it back down: in production it is not advisable to leave that level.

docs.title: Priority of custom fields in alerts
docs.text:
When the same field (_field1_ to _field20_) is defined in several places, the alert engine applies this order of precedence:

Alert type Order of precedence Conventional alerts action > alert template SNMP alerts SNMP alert configuration > action > command default values

In conventional alerts, whatever is defined in the action overrides what comes in the template. In SNMP alerts, the SNMP alert configuration has the highest priority; if it is empty, the value of the action is taken, and as a last resort the default values of the command.

docs.title: WUX modules that do not initialise
docs.text:
WUX modules (Web User Experience) run web transactions in a real web client through Selenium. The periodic checks are performed by the Pandora FMS internal WUX Server. If the modules are left uninitialised, check:

  1. The WUX server is enabled on the server. In /etc/pandora/pandora_server.conf, the wuxserver token must be at 1 (by default it comes disabled at 0).
  2. Connectivity with Selenium. The Pandora FMS server must reach the host and port configured in wux_host and wux_port (by default localhost:4444).
  3. The Pandora FMS server log (pandora_server.log and pandora_server.error) and Selenium's own log, where session or transaction failures are detailed.

docs.title: "Console and server in a different version"
docs.text:
That notice appears when the console and the server are not in the same version. Even if the platform works, it is not a healthy situation: they have to be aligned.

  • The console version is seen in the console footer.
  • The server version, in Servers → Manage servers.

The right thing is to update both to the same version; the order is in Updates.

docs.title: Making the server start up on its own after a crash
docs.text:
In modern systemd distributions, the pandora_server.service service itself includes an automatic restart directive (Restart=always) through the daemon supervisor. To make sure that the service starts with the operating system and recovers if the process goes down:

systemctl enable --now pandora_server
systemctl status pandora_server

In multi-host high availability deployments (active/passive cluster), Pandora FMS also has the cluster tool pandora_ha, which watches the database heartbeat of the nodes and manages the switchover according to the high availability runbook.

docs.title: What licence do I have
docs.text:
The licence type and its expiry date are checked in the console itself, in Management → Setup → License (Licence). That screen is the one that rules: it shows the contracted limit, what is in use and which modality is active.

The possible models (perpetual or subscription, by agents or by modules) and which pieces need a separate licence are explained in Licensing. Here there is no talk of prices or commercial tiers.

docs.title: The licence has expired: how to renew it
docs.text:
The process is the same as the one for the first installation, with the new key:

  1. The provider sends the AuthKey for the new period.
  2. In the console, go to Management → Setup → License and choose Request new license.
  3. Enter the AuthKey in the authentication key field and press the online validation.

The console generates the licence, validates it against the server and leaves it installed. If the installation has no internet access, the same dialog allows activating it by hand; the complete procedure is in Licensing.

docs.title: I have updated and I want to go back
docs.text:
There is no supported way back. An update is not undone by reinstalling the old packages: if something went wrong, what is done is restoring the backup or the machine snapshot, which is exactly what is asked for before starting (see Updates).

That is why the usual recommendation: snapshot before touching anything, and the update in a window with room to go back to the starting point.

Notice

Reinstalling old packages "on top" leaves the installation in a state that is not supported. If there is a need to go back, restore the complete copy or snapshot, including the database and the console files.

docs.title: Modules and network
docs.text:
The checks and the network protocol: modules that do not start or do not answer, ICMP, WMI, SNMP and traps.

A module stores a single metric and its value is interpreted by thresholds. Almost every problem in this section is a matter of the module's own configuration or of a check that does not get to run properly.

docs.title: I cannot change the type of a module
docs.text: It is the behaviour of the product: once created, the type of a module cannot be changed. If you got the type wrong, the module has to be deleted and created again, and its history is lost with it. That is why it pays to get it right the first time, or to try the definition on a test agent before taking it to production.

docs.title: Can local modules be used in templates?
docs.text: No. Module templates are for network components. To apply local modules to many agents at once there are policies, which also carry alerts and also accept network modules.

docs.title: Ping (ICMP) modules do not work
docs.text:
The network problem is separated from the processing one:

Network. The machine is off or offline; there is a cut in the segment; or an intermediate element (firewall, proxy) blocks ICMP. From the server, ping or fping to the destination tells whether the problem is in the network.

Processing. If the module interval is very low, the runs queue up and the module does not arrive in time. It also drags if the server is queued in general. Measure before lowering intervals: since version 784 ICMP supports up to 15 seconds, but that comes at a cost on large machines.

docs.title: An ICMP module is critical even though there is connectivity
docs.text:
Pandora FMS does not use the classic ping: it uses fping, which is more efficient. The server's icmp_checks token decides how many pings it launches per module and comes at 1 by default, so only the first one counts. If the network loses the first packet now and then, the module goes critical for no reason.

Raise it to a higher value so that the result does not depend on a single attempt.

docs.title: WMI modules do not work
docs.text:
WMI has to be enabled on the Windows machine, not only in Pandora FMS:

  1. Open Computer Management → Services and Applications → WMI Control.
  2. In the namespace properties (you can start with root), on the Security tab, grant the Remote Enable permission to the account used for the queries.
  3. Allow it through the Windows firewall.

In Pandora FMS, the default WMI client is pandorawmic, configurable with the server's wmi_client token. It needs the credentials of a user with permissions on the machine being queried.

docs.title: WMI does not work from a satellite server
docs.text: When the satellite server runs as a local user on Windows, some remote WMI queries fail for security reasons. The solution is to run the satellite service with an administrator account of the domain or of the machine. It is changed in the service properties, or with sc.exe config, and the service is restarted.

docs.title: The web check is critical and the website works
docs.text:
Three usual causes:

  • The Pandora FMS server cannot reach the URL: DNS, proxy or firewall.
  • The content has changed and no longer matches the string the module looks for (check_string). A redesign of the page breaks the module even if the service is perfect.
  • The connection is cut halfway through (a proxy with authentication, for example).

To see what is happening exactly, debugging is added to the module itself:

task_begin
get https://www.example.com
cookie 1
resource 1
check_string <string_that_must_appear>
debug /tmp/request.log
task_end

When it runs again, the file shows the error in detail.

docs.title: SNMP interfaces are up but the console shows them down
docs.text:
Before touching the module, confirm that the data arrives:

  • Query the status from the server with snmpget or with the console's SNMP browser. If it shows as up there and not in the module, the problem is in the module.
  • Check the server load. With few resources, SNMP checks are lost and the status you see is the last one that arrived, not the real one.

docs.title: The _modulegraph_nh_ macro does not work
docs.text: That macro inserts the module graph into an alert email, and to draw it the console requests the image from itself. If it comes out broken, access to the API is missing. The API password has to be defined in the console (Management → Settings → System Settings → General setup) and console_api_pass has to be uncommented in the server configuration, with the same password.

docs.title: WMIC and PandoraWMIC
docs.text:
WMIC is the WMI command-line interface that comes with Windows. Pandora FMS uses it only to query (for example, PROCESS GET NAME returns the running processes), never to change anything on the machine.

PandoraWMIC is the client the server uses by default (wmi_client pandorawmic), designed for those monitoring queries.

docs.title: A server plugin does not initialise
docs.text:
Server plugins run on the Pandora FMS server itself, just as they are configured in Servers → Plugins. To debug it, it is launched by hand in the terminal with the same user the server runs as (by default root) and the same parameters.

The output has to be a single datum, and of the type declared when creating the module (numeric or alphanumeric). If the type does not match, the module does not start (the exception is the incremental type, which shows the output as it is). Also, the command must finish without errors: if the errorlevel is not 0, the server discards the result.

docs.title: The agent sends data but it does not show up in the console
docs.text:
It is usually the time. If the clock of the machine where the agent runs is off, the timestamps appear shifted with respect to the server and the data can be hard to find in the view or in the graphs.

Check the offset between the two machines and synchronise them over NTP. Then, check the next interval and look at the server log if the data still does not show up.

docs.title: Adding a MIB to Pandora FMS
docs.text: MIBs are loaded from the Web console itself. In the SNMP monitoring menu there is the MIB loading section (Monitoring → SNMP → MIB uploader). From there, as many files as needed are uploaded, one after another. A MIB is a text file. It can be opened with any editor to check that it is the one for the right manufacturer and model.

docs.title: After loading the MIB, the console still does not recognise the OIDs
docs.text:
Loading the MIB in the console is not enough: the operating system has to know where it is. Check which directories net-snmp is looking at:

net-snmp-config --default-mibdirs
snmpget -Dparse-mibs 2>&1 | grep directory

If the directory where the MIB was left does not appear in that list, move it to one that does. Or add yours to the net-snmp configuration.

docs.title: The SNMP wizard does not find the device OIDs
docs.text:
Before fighting with the wizard, ask the device directly from the server. snmpwalk walks through what it exposes and snmpget requests a specific OID:

snmpwalk -v1 -c 'COMMUNITY' 192.0.2.10
snmpget  -v1 -c 'COMMUNITY' 192.0.2.10 1.3.6.1.2.1.43.5.1.1.1.1.0

Replace COMMUNITY and 192.0.2.10 with the values of your device.

If the device answers these commands, the problem is in the MIB or in the wizard. If it does not answer, it is in the network or in the SNMP community. And whatever you do in the console makes no difference.

docs.title: The traps do not arrive
docs.text:
The first place to look is the Pandora FMS trap log:

tail -f /var/log/pandora/pandora_snmptrap.log

If the message "No access configuration - dropping trap" appears, the trap daemon has its access configured but does not authorise that community. It is fixed by adding the community to the snmptrapd configuration file and restarting:

echo "authCommunity log <configured_community>" >> /etc/snmp/snmptrapd.conf
systemctl restart pandora_server

The community must match the one the device sends. Do not use public in production unless that is really the configured community.

Also, the Pandora FMS SNMP console server comes disabled by default: check that in /etc/pandora/pandora_server.conf the snmpconsole token is at 1. A stopped internal server gives no error, it simply does not do its job.

docs.title: "couldn't open udp:162"
docs.text:
Port 162 is taken by the operating system's snmptrapd, so Pandora FMS cannot listen. The system trap service is stopped and Pandora FMS is restarted. If it happens again after a restart, the system one is disabled:

systemctl stop snmptrapd
systemctl disable snmptrapd
systemctl restart pandora_server

docs.title: On Debian and Ubuntu only numeric OIDs work
docs.text:
Debian and Ubuntu ship the MIB tree disabled, so their SNMP only understands numeric addresses and the console does not resolve names. It is reconfigured in two steps. First, install the MIB downloader. Then, leave the SNMP configuration file clean (/etc/snmp/snmp.conf, with no active lines).

apt-get install snmp-mibs-downloader

docs.title: Deleting old traps
docs.text:
If what you want is a one-off cleanup, it can be done from Admin tools → DB Interface with a statement on the ttrap table:

SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ttrap WHERE timestamp < '<YYYY-MM-DD 00:00:00>';
DELETE FROM ttrap WHERE timestamp < '<YYYY-MM-DD 00:00:00>';

Replace the date with the right one and review the result of the SELECT before running the DELETE.

So that they do not pile up again, the console has the setting "Max. days before deleting traps" in Management → Settings → System Settings → Performance (token trap_purge). From then on, traps older than that are moved to the historical database and then purged.

docs.title: Alerts and events
docs.text: This section gathers the problems that repeat the most with alerts. Sometimes they do not fire when they should. Other times they fire too much. And other times the notice does not arrive in good shape. All the checks are done from the Web console, in Alerts and Management → Settings, except where something else is indicated.

docs.title: The alert does not fire even though the value is bad
docs.text:
It is almost always the minimum number of alerts of the template. That field says how many bad values in a row are needed to fire. The count is this:

  • With minimum 0, the alert fires on the first bad value.
  • With minimum 1, two bad values are needed within the period set by the time threshold.

If the module reports isolated spikes and the alert does not fire, the minimum is set correctly. The problem is not the alert: it is that the module oscillates. Lower the minimum to 0 or adjust the threshold period. And check the module's Flip Flop protection: it requires several checks in a row before changing status.

docs.title: Neither alerts nor events are triggered
docs.text:
Before touching the template, rule out that something is silencing them. It is checked in this order:

  • The Event storm protection is not active in Management → Settings → System Settings → General setup. If it is, the platform dampens events when they arrive in a flood and it may seem that they are not triggered.
  • The agent is not in quiet mode.
  • The module is not either.
  • The group the agent belongs to does not have alerts or events disabled.

If the four things are fine, the alert has to fire. Check the server log to see whether the event is evaluated at all.

docs.title: The alert fires every five minutes
docs.text: The template has two limits that are worth telling apart: the maximum number of alerts and the time threshold. For a problem that persists to warn only once a day: time threshold at one day, minimum at 0 and maximum at 1. That way the alert fires on the first bad value. And it does not repeat until the threshold has passed, however long the module stays bad.

docs.title: What each limit of the template means
docs.text:
The three fields are easily confused and they do different things:

Field What it controls Minimum number of alerts How many times the condition must repeat for the action to run the first time Maximum number of alerts How many alerts can be sent in a row within the same interval Time threshold Time that must pass, with the wrong status still active, before warning again

An example with the threshold at 24 hours. The alert warns once. It does not repeat until a day has passed, even if the module stays in a bad state all that time.

docs.title: The alert email arrives without line breaks
docs.text:
It is a formatting problem of the message body, not of the sending. In the alert action (or in the advanced fields of the template if they are defined there), the text has to be wrapped between the <pre> and </pre> tags:

<pre>
Hello, this is an automated email coming from Pandora FMS

This alert has been fired because a CRITICAL condition in one of your monitored items:

Agent: _agent_
Module: _module_
Module description: _moduledescription_
Timestamp: _timestamp_
Current value: _data_

Thanks for your time.
Best regards,
Pandora FMS.
</pre>

The macros (_agent_, _module_, _data_ and the rest) are replaced on sending. Without the tags, the email client joins all the lines.

docs.title: The graph does not appear in the alert email
docs.text:
The graphs attached to the notices are rendered by the server with a headless rendering engine. If they do not come out, it is checked in this order:

  1. The engine binary is installed and correctly pointed to. The setting is Chromium path in Management → Settings → System Settings → General setup, and by default it is /usr/bin/chromium-browser. If the engine is not installed on the server, there is no graph.
  2. The API configuration is correct. Check the API call the console uses to request the graph.
  3. Name resolution (DNS). If the console calls itself by a name that does not resolve, the API fails. To settle the question, use its IP address.
  4. What is outside: a proxy or a firewall in between.
  5. What is inside: SELinux and iptables on the server itself.

Notice

The old procedure talked about PhantomJS. That engine is no longer used: rendering is done by Chromium, with the Chromium path setting.

docs.title: Reports, logs and email
docs.text: This section gathers the incidents about reports, collections, the log viewer and email.

docs.title: PDF reports are not generated
docs.text:
The PDF of a report is put together by the console with Chromium in headless mode. So the first thing is not PHP, it is the rendering engine:

  • Check that Chromium is installed on the server.
  • Review the Chromium path setting in Management → Settings → System Settings → General setup: it has to point to the real binary (by default, /usr/bin/chromium-browser).
  • If you have just touched the PHP configuration, restart the web service so that it picks it up.

Notice

Old entries talked about curl and allow_url_fopen to generate the PDFs. That was the previous mechanism: today the report is rendered by Chromium, and that is where you have to look first.

docs.title: Not enough memory when generating a report or when updating
docs.text:
The error you see comes from PHP, not from Pandora FMS:

Fatal error: Allowed memory size of XXXXX bytes exhausted

The limit is raised in php.ini (/etc/php.ini or /etc/php/8.x/apache2/php.ini depending on the system), in the memory_limit variable, and if the process takes too long, also max_execution_time. Then restart the web service.

Do not raise the value without a measure: a huge memory_limit can bring the machine down when several requests coincide. Raise just enough and check.

docs.title: File collections do not work
docs.text:
The agent needs unzip to decompress the collections. On Linux it is a dependency of the agent package, so check that it is installed and that the user the agent runs as finds it in its PATH.

If it still does not apply, look at the collections directory of the agent, /etc/pandora/collections. Each downloaded collection leaves an .md5 file next to its folder:

  • If there is an .md5 without a folder that corresponds to it, delete it.
  • In the next cycle, the agent will download the collection again and decompress it.

On Windows there is nothing to install: unzip travels with the agent.

docs.title: "Unable to create the collection"
docs.text:
When you create a collection from the console, that error is usually about paths or permissions. The two paths the process uses are reviewed:

  • The collections folder of the server: data_in/collections.
  • The attachments folder of the console: the Attachment directory configured in Management → Settings → System Settings → General setup (by default, the attachment of the console).

Both have to exist and be readable and writable by the web server user. If the console attachments path does not match the real one, the collection is not created no matter how good the permissions are.

docs.title: The alerts fire but the email does not arrive
docs.text:
It is reviewed in this order:

  1. Where the email is configured. The console or the server file are valid, but not both at once: if they live together, they overwrite each other.
  2. The credentials of the account. If someone changed the password, the sending stops working with no further notice.
  3. The permissions of the account. Many providers require enabling access from third-party applications.
  4. The server log. With verbosity at 10 the email errors show up in /var/log/pandora/pandora_server.log. If the MTA is Postfix, its trace is in /var/log/maillog.

docs.title: The emails arrive with the wrong sender
docs.text:
The default sender is pandora@localhost, which many mail servers reject. It is changed with the mta_from token of /etc/pandora/pandora_server.conf:

mta_from Pandora FMS <pandora@yourdomain.com>

After the change, the server is restarted.

docs.title: It does not send email with authentication
docs.text:
First check that there is an MTA on the server, that the service is started and that the SMTP port is open. Then, that the email parameters are right in one of the two places:

Token (in pandora_server.conf) What it is for mta_address Mail server address mta_port Port (25 by default) mta_user and mta_pass User and password, if the server asks for them mta_auth Authentication system (LOGIN, PLAIN, CRAM-MD5, DIGEST-MD5) mta_from Sender that the recipient will see

The alternative is to configure it in the console, in Management → Settings → System Settings → General setup, in the email section. We insist: one of the two, not both.

docs.title: Name resolution error when sending email
docs.text:
In the console log an error of this type appears:

PHP Warning: fsockopen(): php_network_getaddresses: getaddrinfo failed:
Temporary failure in name resolution

It is a problem of the DNS of the server, not of Pandora FMS. The name resolution of the system (/etc/resolv.conf) is reviewed, and that the name of the mail server resolves from that machine. Restarting the web service can unblock the sending for a while, but it does not fix the cause.

docs.title: The times do not add up
docs.text:
The mismatch can be in three different layers and it is worth checking all of them before touching anything:

Layer How it is checked System date, and the time zone with timedatectl MySQL SELECT now(); and SELECT @@global.time_zone, @@session.time_zone; PHP A loose file that prints date("Y/m/d H:i:s O e")

Once the layer that is out of step is located, correct it there: the time zone of the system, the one of the database server or the one of PHP. The timestamps may appear shifted in the console; check the server log if data is missing too.

docs.title: The log viewer shows nothing
docs.text:
The logs are stored in OpenSearch. If the viewer is empty, it is checked:

  1. The OpenSearch service is running.
  2. There is connection from the Pandora FMS server to port 9200.
  3. The syslog server is enabled. The syslogserver token comes as 0 by default in pandora_server.conf: without it, nobody processes the logs.
  4. The size of the indexes. Huge indexes make the viewer slow or prevent it from loading; they are reviewed and whatever needs rotating is rotated.

docs.title: Configuring rsyslog for the syslog server
docs.text:
The syslog server needs to receive the logs of the devices in a file and then process them. On the server, rsyslog has to be installed and, in /etc/rsyslog.conf, the reception over UDP and TCP on port 514, in addition to the file where the messages are written.

OpenSearch, not Elasticsearch

Old entries say that the logs are sent to Elasticsearch. The store the current documentation uses is OpenSearch.

docs.title: Integrating a ticketing tool
docs.text:
The usual way is opening and closing incidents with alerts: the alert action calls the tool. An email to the ticketing inbox works, and so does a script or a command line call.

For the incident to also be closed when the service recovers, it is necessary to know the closing method and to save the ticket identifier when creating it, in the database or in an exchange file. That identifier is the only thing the recovery alert needs to close the right ticket.

docs.title: Large environments
docs.text:
Command Center, several nodes and high availability: what changes when the environment grows.

This section gathers the incidents that appear when coordinating several nodes, distributing the load and configuring high availability.

docs.title: The server of a node does not start in a Command Center
docs.text:
The server of each node connects to the database configured in its own pandora_server.conf. If it does not start, check that connection first. For a replication incident at the Command Center, see the question "The events do not arrive at the Command Center" further below.

  1. The database engine of the node is running. Check the MySQL, MariaDB or Percona service that node uses.
  2. The node reaches the host indicated by dbhost. Test the connection from the server of the node itself with the dbname, dbuser and dbhost values of its configuration.
  3. The user can access from that host. If the credentials are correct but the connection is rejected, review the database permissions of the node.

The connection values and the passwords are checked in the configuration file of the server; they are not copied here.

docs.title: Deleting agents in a Command Center in centralized mode
docs.text:
In an environment with centralized management enabled, agent administration between nodes is coordinated from Centralised management → Agent management.

For the definitive deletion of an agent, it is necessary to act according to its origin:

  • If it is an EndPoint, uninstall or stop the service on the machine so that it does not send XML again, and delete it in the console of its node or through the bulk agent operations.
  • If it was discovered by a satellite server or generated by a remote plugin, delete the definition on the satellite or the source check before deleting it in the console.

Deleting an agent only on the screen without stopping its source makes the server create it again as soon as it receives the next data packet.

docs.title: How an agent is deleted
docs.text:
It depends on where the agent comes from, and deleting it in the console is not always enough:

Agent type How it is removed Fake The one created by hand in the console: it is deleted there and that is it EndPoint The one installed on the machine: it is deleted in the console and the EndPoint is uninstalled, if you do not want to see it again Broker It is created by the main agent of the device: if it is deleted only in the console, it will show up again From satellite It is created by a satellite server from its configuration: the definition has to be removed on the satellite From plugin It is generated by a plugin when it runs: as long as the plugin keeps creating that XML, the agent comes back

The general rule is simple: if something else generates the agent, delete it at the source. In the console they can be deleted in batches from the bulk agent operations.

docs.title: Several servers and high availability
docs.text:
Pandora FMS supports several data and network servers against the same database, sharing out the load. With that the number of agents grows without changing product. Three pieces hold the whole together:

  • A well-sized MySQL. It is the usual bottleneck: without memory and without fine tuning, the extra servers are of no use.
  • MySQL cluster for high availability and to share out the load of the database.
  • The high availability tool (pandora_ha), which can watch the server and try to recover it. Its installation and start-up depend on the packaging and on the runbook of the cluster.

The servers of the same installation and their distribution of work are explained in Introduction and architecture.

docs.title: Centralized mode: what it is and what to check before enabling it
docs.text:
Centralized mode allows the Command Center to manage groups of agents, tags, alerts, users, policies and collections in several nodes. It is enabled in Advanced → Metasetup, in the Centralized management option.

Check it twice before enabling it

If the environment had already been running for a while with the Command Center and several nodes separately, it is normal for each one to have different things created (groups, tags, policies). When the mode is enabled, the Command Center becomes the source of configuration. Whatever was in the nodes may end up overwritten or misaligned.

With the environment running, it is worth taking an inventory beforehand of what is in each node, deciding which version is the good one and enabling it in a window, with a backup of all the databases.

docs.title: The events do not arrive at the Command Center
docs.text:
Event replication is configured in each node, not in the Command Center. If the events of a node do not show up above, it is checked:

  1. The data of the replication database in Setup → Enterprise of the node: server, database name and user (replication_dbhost, replication_dbname, replication_dbuser). If they are wrong, the node has nowhere to write.
  2. The connectivity of the node towards that database.
  3. The server log of the node, where each replication leaves its trace (one line for each batch of replicated events). If nothing appears there, the problem is in the configuration. If it appears, but the Command Center does not show them, the problem is in the reading.

In the console of the node itself the date of the last replication can be seen, which is the quickest check.

docs.title: The history of a module is not seen in the Command Center
docs.text:
When the graph of a module is opened in the Command Center and an error of the type "Error connecting to database history at …" appears, the Command Center lacks privileges on the historical database of that node.

The Command Center connects to the history with the user, the host, the password and the database name that the node has configured for its history. The permission is granted on the history machine, to that user and for the IP of the Command Center. If the node changes those data, the permission has to be updated.

The passwords are checked in the configuration of each installation; here they are not published.

docs.title: Recovering a downed node in an HA environment
docs.text:
In high availability, when a node goes down or the network is cut, the slave takes over as master. When the downed node comes back, its database has been left out of sync. It has to be resynchronised from the current master before returning it to service. It is what is known as a "broken node".

The procedure, in short:

  1. Put the downed node in standby in the cluster, so that it does not try to take on work.
  2. Stop its MySQL and set its data directory aside.
  3. Make a copy of the master and restore it on the downed node.
  4. Resynchronise with the cluster and return the node to service.

A DBA operation

This is done with the cluster tools (Percona XtraBackup, and Pacemaker/Corosync for the cluster) and with a window ahead. A wrong step leaves both nodes without service, so it is worth following the high availability runbook and not improvising on a production environment.

The parameters of the high availability service are in the server file: ha_interval, ha_hosts, ha_dbuser and ha_dbpass.

docs.title: Automation and plugins
docs.text:
Making Pandora FMS work on its own: command line, API, macros and plugins.

Two ways of working with Pandora FMS without going through the screen: the CLI, which runs on the server itself, and the API, which is called from outside. Both serve to automate and to do in bulk what by hand would be endless.

docs.title: What the CLI is and how it is used
docs.text:
It is a command line administration tool that runs on the Pandora FMS server. It is used to create and delete users, agents and modules, to configure alerts and policies, to manage events and much more, so it is the natural way to automate tasks with scripts.

It is run on the server with pandora_manage.pl and the server configuration:

/usr/share/pandora_server/util/pandora_manage.pl \
    /etc/pandora/pandora_server.conf OPTION PARAMETERS

Replace OPTION and PARAMETERS with the arguments of the operation you are going to run.

A real example: create a group called "Virtual" inside another one called "Servers":

/usr/share/pandora_server/util/pandora_manage.pl /etc/pandora/pandora_server.conf \
    --create_group 'Virtual' 'Servers'

The list of operations is long (agents, modules, alerts, templates, policies, events, users, profiles, collections, visual consoles…). To see it in full, the script is run without options: it shows the help with the syntax of each one.

docs.title: What the API is and how it is protected
docs.text:
The API is a PHP file of the console that is called over HTTP, with curl or from a web tool. It has three security layers, and all three have to be configured before using it:

  1. Allowed IP addresses. In Management → Settings → System Settings → General setup, the "IP list with API access" field accepts one IP per line. The wildcard * opens the API to anyone, and it is not advisable.
  2. API password. In the same place, the "API password" field.
  3. User credentials. Each call also identifies the Pandora FMS user who makes it, with their password.

As the API password travels in the call itself, it is worth making them over HTTPS so that the channel goes encrypted.

A test call, the simplest one, to check that everything is in its place:

https://console.example.com/pandora_console/include/api.php?info=version

Replace console.example.com with the name of your console.

The passwords are not published here: each installation sets its own in the console.

docs.title: Creating and validating events through the API from another machine
docs.text:
The product brings a tool to launch events against the API from a remote system, without the need to touch the database or to have an EndPoint installed: pandora_revent.pl, in the utilities folder of the server.

./pandora_revent.pl \
    -p https://console.example.com/pandora_console/include/api.php \
    -u 'API_PASSWORD,USER_NAME,USER_PASSWORD' \
    -create_event \
    -name "Event name" -group 0 -type "system" -status 0 -severity 4 \
    -user "USER_NAME" -owner_user "USER_NAME" -source "Commandline" \
    -user_comment "Event comment"

The -u parameter carries the three credentials together, separated by commas: the API password, the user and their password.

The same tool validates events, which is the useful thing to close them from outside:

./pandora_revent.pl -p https://console.example.com/pandora_console/include/api.php \
    -u 'API_PASSWORD,USER_NAME,USER_PASSWORD' -validate_event -id EVENT_ID

Replace the example values with the host and the credentials of your installation.

When run without options, it shows its help with the full syntax.

docs.title: Macros in the alerts
docs.text:
A macro is a string surrounded by underscore characters (_macro_). The console replaces it with a text when it launches the action of an alert. They are used so that the notice says which agent it comes from, which module fired it and with what value, without writing it by hand.

The groups that are used the most:

Group Examples Agent _agentname_ (name), _agentalias_, _address_ (its address), _agentstatus_, _agentos_, _agentgroup_, _agentcustomfield_n_ Module _module_ (name), _data_ (the value that fired), _modulegraph_nh_ (the graph) Alert _alert_name_, _alert_priority_, _alert_text_severity_

The full list is in the help of the console itself. The macros are replaced in the subject and in the body of the action. Without them, each alert would have to carry the message written by hand.

docs.title: Custom macros
docs.text:
Besides the built-in ones, your own can be defined. It is the way for a notice to say something specific to your environment.

They are created in the edition of the module itself, in the "Custom macros" section. Key and value pairs are added, and the key is written between underscore characters. For example:

_key_          _technology_
value          the log system

After that, that macro is referenced in the alert like any other:

The agent reports new content in _technology_

and the console replaces it with the value that that module has configured. As the value lives in the module, each one can carry its own.

docs.title: Agent plugins
docs.text:
An agent plugin is a program or script that runs on the monitored machine. It returns a piece of XML that the agent inserts in the packet it sends to the server. A single plugin can return data from several modules.

It is added in two ways:

  • In pandora_agent.conf, with a line: 
    module_plugin /path/to/plugin
  • From the console, in the configuration of the agent, in the plugins section (the puzzle piece icon): the full path of the plugin is indicated.

From there it works like one more local module. It can be written in any scripting language; if it needs libraries (for example, Java), they have to be distributed with it.

docs.title: Server plugins
docs.text:
A server plugin is a script that runs on the Pandora FMS server itself, not on the monitored machine. It returns a single value (numeric, boolean or text) and parameters can be passed to it.

  • They live by default in /usr/share/pandora_server/util/plugin, and the product already brings a few as an example (for example, iface_bandwith.pl).
  • They are registered in Servers → Plugins: name, type (standard or Nagios), maximum timeout, the command and its parameters (which accept macros).
  • Who runs them: the Heavy Server. There is no pluginserver server to activate, as the old entries said. The Heavy Server comes active by default and takes care of plugins, NCM and inventory.

The quickest way to debug them is to launch them by hand in the terminal, with the same parameters. Almost all of them bring help with -h, -help or without arguments.

The timeout is the usual trap

If the plugin takes longer than the configured timeout, it is cut and the module is left with no data. Measure how long the script takes and leave some margin.

docs.title: The plugin module shows up as "Unknown"
docs.text:
When a plugin defines its own modules, the XML it generates has to respect the module_interval that you have configured. If the plugin does not declare it, the console waits for the data at another pace. The modules end up in Unknown even though the plugin is working.

It is corrected in the plugin itself: that the XML includes the interval with which it runs. It is a small adjustment that prevents a cascade of false unknowns.

docs.title: Monitoring with EndPoints
docs.text: The EndPoint is the software installed inside the machine to be monitored, to get the most out of it: processes, services, files, whatever is only visible from the inside. Pandora FMS maintains three, one in Go, another in Perl and another in C++ for Windows, which share the configuration format and the delivery protocol but differ in what each operating system allows. This chapter covers what an EndPoint does, how to take the first steps with it and how to manage its configuration from the Web console without touching the file by hand every time.

docs.title: What an EndPoint is
docs.text:
An EndPoint does the same thing over and over: it reads its configuration file, runs the modules defined in it, gathers the result into an XML and sends it to the server over Tentacle. That cycle repeats every interval seconds, with no further ambition and no mystery. The complexity, if there is any, lies in deciding which modules to run, not in the delivery mechanism.

Do not confuse two things with similar names. The agent is the logical container that exists in the Web console: a name, some modules, a history. The EndPoint is the process installed on the machine that feeds that agent with data. Most of the time they go hand in hand (one EndPoint, one agent), but the agent can exist with no EndPoint behind it, receiving data another way: remote monitoring (SNMP, WMI, network checks from the server or from a Satellite Server), insertion through the API or a discovery plugin. The question that decides between installing an EndPoint or relying on remote monitoring is simple: do you need something that is only visible from inside the machine (a process, a log file, the real CPU usage, a script of your own), or is what you see from outside enough? The second does not require touching the target machine; the first does.

The EndPoint installation is in Online installation of the EndPoint and its offline variants. Here it is assumed that it is already installed and running.

docs.title: The three EndPoints: Go, Perl and Windows
docs.text:
EndPoint Language Systems Service Configuration Go Go Linux x86_64 systemd (pandora_agent_daemon) /etc/pandora/pandora_agent.conf Unix (Perl) Perl Other Unix: AIX, HP-UX, Solaris, BSD, macOS; and Linux on architectures with no Go binary systemd (pandora_agent_daemon) /etc/pandora/pandora_agent.conf Windows C++ MS Windows PandoraFMSAgent service pandora_agent.conf in the installation folder

On Linux, the Go EndPoint is today the one installed by default and the recommended one, and it has good reasons to be. It is a single self-contained binary, statically compiled and with no external libraries: it asks for no interpreter, no modules and no specific versions of anything installed on the machine. The little it uses from the system are the tools every Linux brings as standard (sh, ps, df) and the Tentacle client, which travels in the same package. That makes it ideal to deploy at scale on the systems it is compatible with: you copy it, you start it and it works, with no dependency surprises from one machine to another. And since Go cross-compiles for many operating systems and architectures, the same code can produce binaries for other platforms without rewriting anything; today the official package is distributed for Linux x86_64.

One binary, zero dependencies

To deploy EndPoints on many Linux x86_64 machines, the Go EndPoint is the most convenient option: there is no need to prepare the system before installing it.

The Perl EndPoint comes into play in two situations: Unix systems that are not Linux (AIX, HP-UX, Solaris, the BSDs, macOS) and Linux architectures for which there is no Go binary, which today are x86, armv7l and aarch64. The online installer detects the architecture on its own and switches to building Perl from sources without it having to be asked for explicitly. On Windows, the only candidate is the native C++ EndPoint.

All three speak the same language towards the server: same pandora_agent.conf format, same module_begin / module_end syntax, same data XML and same Tentacle transport. What changes from one to another (which module types it supports, whether it has a watchdog, how it is restarted) is pointed out section by section as it appears.

docs.title: First steps with a freshly installed EndPoint
docs.text:
A freshly installed EndPoint registers the agent in the Web console as soon as it sends its first XML: there is no need to create it by hand. Agent autocreation on the server makes it possible (autocreate 1 in pandora_server.conf), and it comes enabled by default in every environment. The agent appears in the group the EndPoint declares (if that group does not exist, in the fallback group set by autocreate_group on the server) with the interval and the modules that the configuration template brings from the factory: on Linux and Windows, a handful of basic modules (CPU load, TCP connections and plugins for disk, memory and network usage), enough to check at a glance that the delivery works. The default interval is 300 seconds (five minutes); changing it is a matter of editing interval in the configuration file.

If the agent does not appear

With autocreate 0 on the server, the data of an agent that does not exist in the console is discarded. It is a security option for environments where only agents created by hand are accepted; if the EndPoint sends and the agent does not appear, it is the first thing to check.

On Linux, the EndPoint runs as a systemd service named pandora_agent_daemon:

systemctl start pandora_agent_daemon
systemctl stop pandora_agent_daemon
systemctl restart pandora_agent_daemon

The old start-up script in /etc/init.d is still present in some package, but it is retired: it only warns that systemctl has to be used and ends without doing anything. Do not use it, and do not document procedures around it.

On Windows, the EndPoint runs as the PandoraFMSAgent service:

NET START PandoraFMSAgent
NET STOP PandoraFMSAgent

The configuration lives in /etc/pandora/pandora_agent.conf on Linux and Unix (the same file for the Go EndPoint and the Perl one; in an installation with its own path, in <prefix>/etc/pandora/) and in pandora_agent.conf inside the installation folder on Windows (by default, C:\Program Files\pandora_agent). Any manual change to that file requires restarting the service for it to take effect; if remote configuration is active, bear in mind what is explained further down too, because a local change may end up overwritten.

docs.title: Essential parameters of pandora_agent.conf
docs.text:
Of the many tokens pandora_agent.conf accepts, these are the ones touched on the first day. The rest (modules aside) is in the full EndPoint configuration reference.

Parameter What it does Default server_ip IP or FQDN of the Pandora FMS server the EndPoint reports to. localhost interval Seconds between each collection and delivery cycle. 300 group Group the agent is assigned to in the Web console. No value in the code; the installation templates bring Servers. agent_alias Visible name of the agent in the console. If left empty, it takes the machine name (hostname). Do not confuse it with agent_name, the internal identifier the server uses to avoid duplicating agents: changing the alias does not rename the agent. Empty (hostname) remote_config Allows editing this configuration and its modules from the console. It is covered in detail in the next section. 0 in the code; the installation templates leave it at 1 debug With 1, the EndPoint logs more detail in its log and, after sending each XML, keeps a copy in the temporary folder (with the sent suffix) instead of deleting it. The data is sent anyway: it serves to see exactly what is sent, not to test on the sly. 0

docs.title: Remote configuration from the Web console
docs.text:
It comes enabled from the factory

The Linux and Windows installation templates bring remote_config 1: any EndPoint installed with the standard package allows, from the first minute, someone with access to the console to edit its configuration and its modules without touching the machine. The online installer only changes that value if the PANDORA_REMOTE_CONFIG variable is passed to it explicitly; if nothing is touched, it stays active. If the remote_config token is missing from the file altogether, the value the code assumes is 0, but that is not what the standard installation brings: it is the situation of a file edited by hand and trimmed. Before taking for granted that an EndPoint is closed to remote changes, check the token.

With remote configuration active, the console can replace the EndPoint pandora_agent.conf entirely and create or modify local modules without anyone connecting to the machine. The mechanism underneath is the same in all three EndPoints, with nuances: on each cycle, the EndPoint calculates the MD5 of its current configuration and compares it with the one on the server.

  • If the server does not have an MD5 for that agent yet, the EndPoint uploads its local configuration: it is the first contact, and the console starts from what was already on the machine instead of demanding that it be written from scratch.
  • If the server MD5 differs from the local one, the EndPoint downloads the new configuration and leaves it as its active file.
  • If they match, nothing happens: it is the normal case, cycle after cycle.

Deactivating it is as simple as setting remote_config 0 and restarting the service; from then on, changes only get in by editing the file by hand on the machine.

Two more pieces of the configuration worth knowing from the start: the agent custom fields, which the EndPoint can declare in its file (custom_field1_name, custom_field1_value and so on) and which, with remote configuration active, are also edited from the console; and the password-protected groups: if the console group requires a password, the EndPoint has to declare it with group_password for the server to create the agent in that group.

A custom field is only filled in if it already exists in the console with that same name (Resources → Custom fields); if it does not exist, the server discards the value outright. Its type is also defined there: free text, list of values, password (the console shows it with asterisks) or link. For a field of type link, the EndPoint sends a pair with the text and the address:

custom_field1_name Documentation
custom_field1_value ["Server manual","https://intranet.example.com/srv01"]

A difference between EndPoints, and not a small one: the Perl EndPoint applies remote configuration with any transfer_mode (tentacle, ssh, ftp or local), while the Go EndPoint only does so with tentacle or local; with ssh or ftp it does not download remote configuration.

docs.title: EndPoint autoconfiguration
