docs.title: Full EndPoint configuration reference
docs.text: Raw technical reference for pandora_agent.conf: every general token and every module token, with its compatibility by EndPoint (Go, Perl, Windows). It is looked up, not read from cover to cover. The explanations and the examples are in 2.1 · Monitoring with EndPoints, which this page links to.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
This reference gathers, table by table, every pandora_agent.conf token recognised by the three Pandora FMS EndPoints: the Go EndPoint, the Perl EndPoint (Linux/Unix) and the Windows EndPoint. For each token it states its description, its syntax or default value, and whether the Go EndPoint, the Perl EndPoint and the Windows EndPoint accept it.

pandora_agent.conf is located in:

EndPoint Path Go and Perl (Linux/Unix) /etc/pandora/pandora_agent.conf. Both use the same file at the same path. With an installation in a custom path, the configuration stays in <prefix>/etc/pandora/; on FreeBSD and NetBSD, the installer already uses /usr/local/etc/pandora. Windows C:\Program Files\pandora_agent\pandora_agent.conf

The file syntax is the same in the three EndPoints: one token per line, comments with #, and module tokens grouped in module_begin / module_end blocks (except module_plugin, which can also go loose on a single line, outside any block). General tokens are valid anywhere in the file, outside a module block.

For explanations, examples and the reason behind each token, see 2.1 · Monitoring with EndPoints.

docs.title: General tokens
docs.text: Tables by topic:

docs.title: Server connection
docs.text: Token Description Value / default Go Perl Windows server_ip Address or name of the Pandora FMS server (Tentacle, FTP, SSH or local directory) the EndPoint sends the data XML to. Text. localhost by default. Yes Yes Yes server_port TCP port of the server for the chosen transfer mode (Tentacle 41121, SSH 22, FTP 21). Integer. 41121 by default. Yes Yes Yes server_user Remote user for the FTP/SSH transfer modes. Text. pandora by default. Yes Yes No server_pwd Password for Tentacle (if the server requires it) or for FTP/SSH. Text. Empty by default. Yes Yes Yes server_ssl Turns on OpenSSL in the Tentacle client. yes/no or 1/0. 0/no by default (off). Yes Yes Yes server_opts Additional options added literally to the command line of the transfer client (for example -v -r 5 for Tentacle). Free text. Empty by default. Yes Yes Yes server_path Remote path (data_in) where the server waits for the data XML. Text. /var/spool/pandora/data_in by default. Yes Yes Yes server_path_conf Remote subdirectory used by remote configuration to drop the new .conf. Text. conf by default. Perl and Go only. Yes Yes No server_path_md5 Remote subdirectory used by remote configuration for the change control .md5. Text. md5 by default. Perl and Go only. Yes Yes No server_path_ref Remote reference subdirectory for the .md5/.conf files of remote configuration; only the Perl EndPoint uses it. Text. ref by default. Perl only. No Yes No server_path_zip Remote subdirectory where the server serves the compressed collections. Text. collections by default. Perl and Go only. Yes Yes No transfer_mode Transfer method of the data XML to the primary server. tentacle (default), ftp, ssh or local. Go supports only tentacle and local. Yes Yes Yes transfer_mode_user Owner user of the copied files when transfer_mode is local. Text. apache by default. Perl and Go only. Yes Yes No transfer_timeout Maximum time, in seconds, for the transfer program to complete the delivery before it is taken as failed. Integer. 30 by default. Yes Yes Yes

docs.title: Agent identification
docs.text: Token Description Value / default Go Perl Windows agent_name Unique name of the logical agent in the console. If it is omitted, the host name is used. Text. The hostname by default. Yes Yes Yes agent_name_cmd Command whose first output line is used as agent_name; the special value __rand__ generates a persistent random name. Text (shell command) or __rand__. Empty by default. Yes Yes Yes agent_alias Agent alias shown in the console (it does not have to be unique). Text. The hostname by default. Yes Yes Yes agent_alias_cmd Command whose first output line is used as agent_alias. Text (shell command). Empty by default. Yes Yes Yes group Console group the agent belongs to. Text. Empty by default. Yes Yes Yes group_id Numeric identifier of the group, an alternative to the name (group). Integer. Undefined by default. Yes Yes Yes custom_field<n>_name / custom_field<n>_value Custom field number <n> of the agent: field name and value sent in the XML (<custom_fields>). Text. <n> = 1, 2, 3… Undefined by default. Yes Yes Yes group_password Group password, if the group requires it for the automatic creation of the agent. Text. Undefined by default. Yes Yes Yes address IP address reported as the one of the agent; the special value auto makes the EndPoint detect it locally. Text or auto. Undefined by default. Yes Yes Yes description Free description of the agent, shown in the console. Text. Empty by default. Yes Yes Yes custom_id Free external identifier of the agent (for integrations). Text. Empty by default. Yes Yes Yes url_address URL linked to the agent, shown as a link in the console. Text. Empty by default. Yes Yes Yes latitude Fixed latitude of the agent GIS position (if gis_exec is not used). Decimal. Undefined by default. Yes Yes Yes longitude Fixed longitude of the agent GIS position (if gis_exec is not used). Decimal. Undefined by default. Yes Yes Yes altitude Fixed altitude of the agent GIS position. Decimal. Undefined by default. Yes Yes Yes position_description Text description of the GIS position (for example "Madrid, city centre"). Text. Undefined by default. Yes Yes Yes gis_exec Script that, when run, returns latitude,longitude[,altitude]; if it is defined and exists, it takes priority over the fixed latitude/longitude/altitude. Path to an executable. Undefined by default. Yes Yes Yes parent_agent_name Name of the parent agent, to build agent hierarchies in the console. Text. Undefined by default. Yes Yes Yes secondary_groups Additional secondary groups of the agent, separated by commas. Text (comma-separated list). Undefined by default. Yes Yes Yes encoding Encoding declared in the header of the data XML. Text. Perl and Go use UTF-8 by default; Windows uses ISO-8859-1 by default. Yes Yes Yes timezone_offset Time difference, in hours, between the agent and the server. Integer. 0 by default. Yes Yes No

docs.title: Execution
docs.text: Token Description Value / default Go Perl Windows interval Interval, in seconds, between two full runs of the agent (XML deliveries). Integer. 300 by default. Yes Yes Yes intensive_interval Interval, in seconds, for the modules in intensive mode (with module_intensive_condition); if it is not defined, it takes the value of interval. Integer. Equal to interval by default. Yes Yes Yes debug Debug mode: the agent keeps generating and sending data, but it keeps a copy of every XML sent with the .datasent suffix instead of deleting it, and the check of remote configuration and collections is skipped in that cycle. 0/1. 0 by default. Yes Yes Yes logfile Path of the agent log file. Path. /var/log/pandora/pandora_agent.log by default (Linux). Perl and Go only. Yes Yes No logsize Maximum size, in bytes, of the log before it is rotated. Integer. 600000 by default. Perl and Go only. Yes Yes No logrotate Number of rotated copies of the log that are kept. Integer. 3 by default. Perl and Go only. Yes Yes No disable_logfile Turns off the writing of the agent log. 0/1. 0 by default (log on). Windows only. No No Yes pandora_user System user the Perl agent process runs as (it drops privileges after starting as root). System user name. Undefined by default (root). Yes Yes No pandora_nice Priority (nice) of the agent process; higher values give more CPU back to the rest of the system. Integer. 10 by default. Yes Yes No pandora_exec Wrapper used to run the module commands under module_timeout control. Path to an executable. pandora_agent_exec by default. Perl only. No Yes No cron_mode Replaces the agent own loop with a single run per invocation, meant to be launched from the system cron. 0/1. 0 by default (off; turning it on is not recommended unless there is a specific need). Yes Yes No delayed_startup Seconds the agent waits before the first run at start-up. Integer (seconds). 0 by default. Name equivalent to startup_delay on Windows. Yes Yes No startup_delay Seconds the agent waits before the first run at start-up. Integer (seconds). 0 by default. Windows only; equivalent to delayed_startup in Perl/Go. No No Yes agent_threads Number of threads used to run modules in parallel. Integer. 1 by default. Yes Yes No autotime If it is on, the agent does not include a timestamp in the XML, and it is the server that assigns the arrival time. 0/1. 0 by default. Yes Yes Yes standby Standby mode: the agent keeps running its cycle but it does not run modules or send data to the server, unless debug is on. 0/1. 0 by default. Yes Yes Yes

docs.title: XML transfer and buffer
docs.text: Token Description Value / default Go Perl Windows xml_buffer Turns on the XML buffer: if the delivery to the server fails, the data is saved in temporal and retried in later cycles instead of being lost. 0/1. 0 by default in the binary; the installation templates turn it on (1). Yes Yes Yes temporal Working directory of the agent for temporary files and, with the buffer on, for the XML waiting to be sent. Path. /var/spool/pandora by default (Perl/Go) or %ProgramFiles%\pandora_agent\temp (Windows). Yes Yes Yes temporal_min_size Minimum free space, in megabytes, in temporal for remote configuration and the XML buffer to be accepted; below this threshold they are skipped. Integer (MB). 1024 by default (Perl/Go). Yes Yes Yes temporal_max_size Maximum total size, in megabytes, the XML buffer can take. Integer (MB). 1024 by default. Yes Yes Yes temporal_max_files Maximum number of XML files the buffer can gather. Integer. 1024 by default. Yes Yes Yes

docs.title: Secondary server
docs.text: Token Description Value / default Go Perl Windows secondary_mode When the data is also sent to a secondary server: never (never), on_error (only if the primary fails) or always (always, in addition to the primary). never (default), on_error or always. Yes Yes Yes secondary_server_ip Address of the secondary server. Text. localhost by default. Yes Yes Yes secondary_server_path Remote data path on the secondary server, equivalent to server_path. Text. /var/spool/pandora/data_in by default. Yes Yes Yes secondary_server_port Port of the secondary server. Integer. 41121 by default. Yes Yes Yes secondary_server_pwd Transfer password for the secondary server. Text. Empty by default. Yes Yes Yes secondary_server_ssl Turns on OpenSSL in the Tentacle connection to the secondary server. yes/no or 1/0. 0/no by default. Yes Yes Yes secondary_server_user Remote user for the secondary server in FTP/SSH modes. Text. pandora by default. Perl and Go only. Yes Yes No secondary_server_opts Additional options for the transfer client to the secondary server, equivalent to server_opts. Free text. Empty by default. Yes Yes Yes secondary_temporal Directory of the XML waiting for the secondary server. It is not configured in practice: the EndPoint sets it from temporal (temporal/pandorafms.secondary with secondary_mode always, temporal itself with on_error) and discards the value in the file. Path. Derived from temporal. Yes Yes Yes secondary_transfer_mode Transfer mode to the secondary server, equivalent to transfer_mode. tentacle (default), ftp, ssh or local. Yes Yes Yes secondary_transfer_timeout Maximum transfer time to the secondary server. Integer (seconds). 30 by default. Yes Yes Yes

docs.title: Remote configuration and collections
docs.text: Token Description Value / default Go Perl Windows remote_config Lets the web console (Enterprise) overwrite the local pandora_agent.conf; the EndPoint compares the MD5 with the server on every cycle and downloads the file if it changed. 0/1. 0 by default in the code; the installation templates turn it on (1). In Go it works only with transfer_mode tentacle or local. Yes Yes Yes file_collection Registers a file collection (scripts, binaries) that the server distributes and the EndPoint synchronises in collections/. Name of the collection. It can be repeated; one per line. Yes Yes Yes include Includes additional configuration files, of which only module, plugin and collection definitions are read: the general tokens of an included file are ignored. Path or glob pattern. It can be repeated. Yes Yes No cmd_file Registers an allowed remote command (RMM) that the console can invoke on the agent. Name of the command. It can be repeated; one per line. Perl and Go only. Yes Yes No

docs.title: Broker mode and proxy mode
docs.text: Token Description Value / default Go Perl Windows broker_agent Registers a broker agent: an additional agent identity, with its own <name>.conf derived from the main one, run from the same EndPoint. Name of the broker agent. It can be repeated; one per line. Yes Yes Yes proxy_mode Turns on proxy mode: the EndPoint launches a local tentacle_server that forwards to the real server, so that other EndPoints use it as a gateway. It requires a server_ip other than localhost; with localhost, the Perl EndPoint logs the error and exits. 0/1. 0 by default. Yes Yes Yes proxy_address Address the Tentacle listens on in proxy mode. Text. 0.0.0.0 by default. Yes Yes Yes proxy_port Port the Tentacle listens on in proxy mode. Integer. 41121 by default. Yes Yes Yes proxy_max_connection Maximum number of simultaneous connections the proxy accepts. Integer. 10 by default. Yes Yes Yes proxy_timeout Wait time, in seconds, of the Tentacle in proxy mode. Integer. 1 by default. Yes Yes Yes

docs.title: UDP server
docs.text: Token Description Value / default Go Perl Windows udp_server Turns on the internal UDP server, which allows restarting the agent or controlling processes/services remotely. 0/1. 0 by default. No Yes Yes udp_server_address Address the UDP server listens on. Text. Windows only. No No Yes udp_server_auth_address List of IP addresses allowed to send orders to the UDP server, separated by commas; 0.0.0.0 allows any origin. Text (IP or comma-separated list). 0.0.0.0 by default. No Yes Yes udp_server_port Port the UDP server listens on. Integer. 41122 by default (Perl); 4321 in the Windows template example. No Yes Yes process_<name>_start / _stop Defines the command the UDP server runs when it receives the order to start or stop the process <name>. Perl accepts the word order START PROCESS <name> / STOP PROCESS <name>; Windows requires exactly three words, START PROCESS <name> / STOP PROCESS <name>. Shell command (Perl) or program (Windows). Undefined by default. No Yes Yes service_<name> Authorises (with value 1) that the UDP server starts or stops Windows service <name> through the orders START SERVICE <name> / STOP SERVICE <name>. 0/1. Not authorised by default. Windows only. No No Yes

docs.title: Other
docs.text: Token Description Value / default Go Perl Windows agent_mode Learning mode of the agent for new modules: learn (default), do not learn or self-disable. Perl and Windows translate the value to a numeric code (0/1/2); Go limits itself to forwarding the text as it is to the server. learn (default), no-learn/nolearn or autodisable. Yes Yes Yes default_native_encoding Default native encoding (for example OEM) for the output of module_exec/module_plugin when the module does not set its own module_native_encoding. Text (encoding name). Empty by default. Windows only. No No Yes ehorus_conf Path to the configuration file of the Pandora RC agent (formerly eHorus); if it exists, the EndPoint automatically adds a custom field eHorusID with the agent key. Path to a file. Undefined by default. Yes Yes Yes rmm_enabled Starts the Pandora RMM agent (pandora_rmm_agent) together with the EndPoint, using the same configuration file. 0/1. 0 by default. Yes Yes Yes macro<name> General macro: <name> is replaced by its value in the modules of the file. macro<name> <value>. Yes Yes No

docs.title: Module tokens
docs.text: Tables by topic:

docs.title: Module structure
docs.text: Token Description Value / default Go Perl Windows module_begin Opens the definition of a module. Everything that follows up to module_end belongs to that module. No value. Yes Yes Yes module_end Closes the definition of a module started with module_begin. No value. Yes Yes Yes module_name Name of the module, as it appears in the web console. Required except in module_plugin modules, loose or in a block, because the name is set by the plugin itself in its XML. Text. Yes Yes Yes module_type Data type of the module (numeric, incremental, string, proc, log, asynchronous version…), it defines how the server interprets it. Text (for example generic_data, generic_data_string, generic_proc, async_data…). generic_data by default. Yes Yes Yes module_disabled If it is 1, the module is discarded when the configuration is read and it is not run. 0/1. 0 by default. Yes Yes Yes module_source_type Labels the data origin of a log type module (it is included as <source_type> in the XML). Text. syslog by default (Perl). Yes Yes Yes module_native_encoding Native encoding of the output of a specific module_exec/module_plugin; if it is omitted, default_native_encoding is used. Text (encoding name). Empty by default. Windows only. No No Yes module_macro<name> Defines a module macro: <name> is replaced by its value in the rest of the tokens of the module (command, thresholds, conditions…). module_macro<name> <value>. Yes Yes Yes

docs.title: Data gathering: common, Unix (Go and Perl) and Windows
docs.text: Token Description Value / default Go Perl Windows module_exec Runs a shell command; its standard output is the module datum. Shell command. Yes Yes Yes module_exec_powershell Runs a PowerShell script or command; its output is the module datum. PowerShell command. Windows only. No No Yes module_plugin Runs a plugin (script or binary) that returns XML of one or several modules directly; it can go loose (one line, outside module_begin/module_end) or inside a module block. Plugin command and its arguments. Yes Yes Yes module_cpuusage Built-in module: CPU usage percentage. In Go it accepts empty, all or the number of a core; in Windows and Perl, the core number (empty = global). Empty (global) or core number. Yes Yes Yes module_cpuproc Built-in module (Unix): CPU percentage of the given process. If the process is not running, the module generates no datum. Full command line, with exact match, as shown by ps aux. Perl and Go only. Yes Yes No module_memproc Built-in module (Unix): resident memory of the given process, in MB. If the process is not running, the module generates no datum. Full command line, with exact match, as shown by ps aux. Perl and Go only. Yes Yes No module_freememory Built-in module: free memory of the system, in KB. No value. Yes Yes Yes module_freepercentmemory Built-in module: percentage of free memory of the system. No value. Yes Yes Yes module_freedisk Built-in module: free space, in MB, of the given mount point or drive. Mount point on Unix (/var), drive letter on Windows (C:). The Perl EndPoint requires the value; Go uses / if it is missing. Yes Yes Yes module_freepercentdisk Built-in module: percentage of free space of the given mount point. Mount point path or drive. Yes Yes Yes module_occupiedpercentdisk Built-in module: percentage of occupied space of the given mount point. Mount point path. Perl and Go only. Yes Yes No module_proc Built-in process module. On Unix (Perl/Go) it checks an exact match of ps aux and returns 1/0; on Windows it counts the instances of the process and accepts a watchdog. Exact name of the process (Unix) or of the executable (Windows). Yes Yes Yes module_service Alias of module_proc on Unix (same process check); on Windows it checks the status of a service and its watchdog restarts the service itself. Name of the process (Unix) or of the service (Windows). Yes Yes Yes module_proc_cmd Redefines, for the whole file, the system command the proc/service module uses to list processes. Shell command. Perl and Go only. Yes Yes No module_freedisk_cmd Redefines, for the whole file, the system command the freedisk/freepercentdisk module uses to query the space. Shell command. Perl and Go only. Yes Yes No module_inventory Built-in module (Windows): gathers one system inventory block. Deprecated: today inventory is gathered with EndPoint plugins, both on Windows and on Linux and Unix. List of inventory sections. Windows only. No No Yes module_wmiquery WMI query whose result is the module datum (it is combined with module_wmicolumn). WMI query (SELECT … FROM …). Windows only. No No Yes module_wmicolumn Column of the module_wmiquery query taken as the value of the module. WMI column name. Windows only. No No Yes module_perfcounter Reads a Windows performance counter (the counter names are localised by the language of the system). Performance counter path (\object\counter). Windows only. No No Yes module_cooked Indicates that the value of module_perfcounter must be returned "cooked" (already calculated, not raw). 0/1. Windows only. No No Yes module_tcpcheck Checks whether a host accepts a TCP connection on the given port (module_port). Host or IP. Windows only. No No Yes module_port TCP port used by module_tcpcheck. Integer. Windows only. No No Yes module_ping Pings the given address. Host or IP. Windows only. No No Yes module_ping_count Number of ICMP packets to send in module_ping. Integer. 1 by default. Windows only. No No Yes module_ping_timeout Wait time, in milliseconds, of each packet of module_ping. Integer (ms). 1000 by default. Windows only. No No Yes module_snmpget SNMP GET query module. Turns the module on (it is combined with the module_snmp_* tokens). Windows only. No No Yes module_snmp_version SNMP version used by module_snmpget. Text/integer. 1 by default. Windows only. No No Yes module_snmp_community SNMP community used by module_snmpget. Text. public by default. Windows only. No No Yes module_snmp_agent Address of the SNMP agent queried by module_snmpget. Host or IP. localhost by default. Windows only. No No Yes module_snmp_oid OID queried by module_snmpget. OID. Windows only. No No Yes module_advanced_options Additional options passed literally to the internal executable of module_ping or module_snmpget. Free text. Windows only. No No Yes module_retries Number of retries before running module_start_command in a module_proc with watchdog. Integer. Windows only, and only with a process watchdog. No No Yes module_startdelay Wait, in seconds, before the first start attempt in the watchdog of a module_proc. Integer (seconds). Windows only, and only with a process watchdog. No No Yes module_retrydelay Wait, in seconds, between retries of the watchdog of a module_proc. Integer (seconds). Windows only, and only with a process watchdog. No No Yes module_user_session Runs module_start_command in the interactive session of the user, not in the service session. 0/1. Windows only, and only with a process watchdog. No No Yes module_wait_timeout Polling interval while a module_exec is still running: how often the EndPoint checks whether it has finished and reads its output. The total limit is set by module_timeout. Integer (milliseconds). 500 by default. Windows only. No No Yes

docs.title: Thresholds and statuses
docs.text: Token Description Value / default Go Perl Windows module_max Maximum normal value of the numeric datum of the module (visual/graph reference). Numeric. Yes Yes Yes module_min Minimum normal value of the numeric datum of the module. Numeric. Yes Yes Yes module_max_warning Upper limit of the warning range. Numeric. docs.title: Notable differences between EndPoints
docs.text:
• Default XML encoding. Perl and Go use UTF-8; Windows uses ISO-8859-1 (see encoding).
  • A different name for the same concept. The start-up delay is called delayed_startup in Perl and Go, and startup_delay on Windows.
  • Token alias. module_service is an exact alias of module_proc on Unix (same process check); on Windows they are different built-ins (process vs. service), with watchdogs that behave differently.
  • Asymmetric watchdog. The Windows watchdog exists only for module_proc (it needs module_start_command, module_retries, module_startdelay, module_retrydelay, module_user_session) and for module_service (it restarts the service itself, without a recovery command). Neither Perl nor Go implements a watchdog.
  • Asynchronous module only on Windows. module_async exists only in the Windows EndPoint; Perl and Go derive the asynchronous type automatically when a module with module_absoluteinterval runs once.
  • Tokens with a variable name. module_macro<name> (module macros) and custom_field<n>_name / custom_field<n>_value are accepted by the three EndPoints; the general macros macro<name>, only by Perl and Go.
  • UDP server. It exists only in Perl and Windows (not in Go). The format of the orders differs: Perl accepts START PROCESS <name> / STOP PROCESS <name>; Windows requires exactly three words (<order> <action> <target>, for example REFRESH AGENT *, START PROCESS <name>, START SERVICE <name>), and it adds the control of services (service_<name>) that Perl does not have.
  • Remote configuration and transport. The Go EndPoint accepts only remote_config with transfer_mode tentacle or local; Perl accepts it with any transfer mode.
  • Windows-only tokens. All the built-in Windows query modules (module_wmiquery, module_perfcounter, module_snmpget, module_ping, module_tcpcheck, module_logevent/module_logchannel and their filters, module_inventory, module_exec_powershell), in addition to disable_logfile, default_native_encoding, startup_delay and udp_server_address.
  • Unix-only tokens (Perl and Go). module_cpuproc, module_memproc, module_occupiedpercentdisk, module_proc_cmd, module_freedisk_cmd, pandora_user, logfile/logsize/logrotate, cron_mode, agent_threads, cmd_file, include, timezone_offset, pandora_nice, transfer_mode_user and server_path_conf / server_path_md5 / server_path_zip.
  • Token only parsed, with no equivalent in the other two. server_path_ref exists only in the Perl EndPoint (reference directory of the remote configuration).

docs.title: Full console configuration reference
docs.text:
This reference is not read from cover to cover: it is looked up by option name or by tab, like a dictionary. It gathers the whole configuration of the Web console (node and Command Center) and of include/config.php, so that any other chapter can link here instead of repeating a table of options.

Where each thing lives:

  • Web console (Settings → System Settings). Almost all the configuration of behavior, appearance and credentials of external services. It is stored in the database, not in a file: it changes on the fly, without restarting anything.
  • include/config.php. A handful of values that are edited by hand only, before the console can connect to the database: database connection, installation path, encryption passphrase. See § 23.
  • Command Center. A special console that centralizes several nodes. It has its own configuration pages (§ 22) and, in addition, it can set some settings of the nodes it manages centrally.

A node with "centralized management" active in a specific section stops accepting local changes in that section: they are edited from the Command Center and synchronized to the node.

docs.title: Full server configuration reference
docs.text: Raw technical reference for pandora_server.conf: every token the server recognises, with its real default value. It is looked up, not read from cover to cover; any other chapter links here when it needs to refer to a server parameter.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
pandora_server.conf is the only configuration file of the Pandora FMS server. Its path is configurable at installation; by default, /etc/pandora/pandora_server.conf. The format is the usual one: one token per line, value after a space, and # to comment a whole line or to leave an example token disabled.

A change in the file is not applied on the fly: the service has to be restarted.

systemctl restart pandora_server

The exception is remote configuration: with remote_config 1 (see "Remote configuration, Tentacle and synchronization", further down), the whole file can be edited from the web console. The server checks now and then whether there are changes; when it finds them, it generates a restart event, reloads the configuration and restarts itself.

The tokens exclusive to the satellite servers (pandora_satellite.conf) are not in this reference: they have their own chapter, 6.2 · Satellite servers, which links here for what they share with the main server.

The "default value" of each table is the one the server itself applies when the token does not appear in the file. The sample template shipped with the package (pandora_server.conf.new) does not always match that value: when it differs in a relevant way, the table says so explicitly, never as if it were "the" default value.

docs.title: Full Tentacle reference (server and client)
docs.text: Raw technical reference for the Tentacle protocol and its two implementations (Go and Perl). It is looked up, not read from cover to cover; the rest of the site links here for any option or token of the Tentacle binary. For the EndPoint connection tokens (server_ip, server_opts…), see 9.1 · Full EndPoint configuration reference; for the tokens of the synchronization server that use Tentacle underneath, see 9.3 · Full server configuration reference.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
Tentacle is both a file transfer protocol and the client/server tool that speaks it. It replaced SCP/FTP in 2008 as the default method for sending the data XML of the EndPoints, and it is assigned IANA port tcp/41121.

In the product, Tentacle carries: the data XML sent by each EndPoint, the remote configuration files, the collections, the remote commands (RMM), the traffic of the satellite servers, the Tentacle proxy and the dedicated RMM instance.

There are two implementations of the same protocol, with the same command-line options (same letter, same meaning):

  • Go (static tentacle_server/tentacle_client binary, with no runtime dependencies): it is the default implementation in the Linux packages (server, EndPoint and satellite server) and the recommended one. It handles each connection with a goroutine instead of Perl's busy-waiting thread.
  • Perl (tentacle_server v0.6.2, tentacle_client v0.4.0): the historical reference implementation of the protocol. It is the one still shipped, compiled to .exe, by the Windows packages (EndPoint and satellite server).

They are interchangeable: a Perl client talks to a Go server and vice versa, because both implement the same protocol with the same rules.

The chapter is divided into three blocks: the protocol itself (independent of the implementation), the client and the server.

docs.title: 1. The Tentacle protocol
docs.text:
The design is deliberately simple:

  • The client always starts the connection; the server never sends data before the client asks for it or confirms it.
  • Commands are text terminated by a line break. There is no greeting or version negotiation: the first message the client sends is already a command.
  • When a command announces a size (SIZE <n>), a binary block of exactly that number of bytes follows, with no padding or additional header.

docs.title: Command table
docs.text:
Command Direction Successful response Errors SEND <file> SIZE <n> Client → server SEND OK (accept confirmation) and SEND OK (received confirmation) SEND ERR (invalid file name), SEND ERR (file is too big), SEND ERR (file already exists), SEND ERR (upload not allowed) ZSEND <file> SIZE <n> Client → server, compressed ZSEND OK (accept) and ZSEND OK (received) ZSEND ERR (invalid file name), ZSEND ERR (file is too big), ZSEND ERR (file already exists), ZSEND ERR (upload not allowed), ZSEND ERR (failed to decompress) RECV <file> Client ← server RECV SIZE <n>, then the client replies RECV OK and the server sends the data RECV ERR (file has an invalid file name), RECV ERR (file does not exist), SEND ERR (download not allowed) ZRECV <file> Client ← server, compressed same as RECV with the ZRECV prefix ZRECV ERR (file has an invalid file name), ZRECV ERR (file does not exist), SEND ERR (download not allowed) LS <filter> Client ← server (insecure mode) LS SIZE <n>, the client replies LS OK and the server sends the listing LS ERR (filter with an invalid name, or when opening the directory) MV <file> Client ← server (insecure mode) MV SIZE <n>, the client replies MV OK, the server sends the file and deletes it MV ERR (invalid name or does not exist), SEND ERR (download not allowed) (not allowed) PASS <digest> Client → server PASS OK the server closes the connection without a message if the password does not match QUIT Client → server closes the connection without a response — Unrecognized command — — the server logs Unknown command '<command>' and closes the connection, without notifying the client

The "download not allowed" notice always reuses the string SEND ERR (download not allowed), whether the operation is RECV, ZRECV or MV: both implementations share this quirk inherited from the protocol, it is not a transcription error.

docs.title: Sending files (SEND)
docs.text:
The client announces SEND <name> SIZE <n>. The server checks, in this order, whether the destination allows upload (according to download_only), whether the name is valid, whether the size is between 1 byte and the configured maximum, and whether a file with that name already exists (with overwrite off). A file of size 0 is rejected with the same message as one that is too big (SEND ERR (file is too big)): it is the normal behavior of the protocol, not a quirk of one implementation. After a successful transfer, the client can send a new SEND (or another command) in the same session; the final close is marked by QUIT.

Client:   SEND <report.xml> SIZE 1024
Server:   SEND OK
Client:   <1024 bytes of data>
Server:   SEND OK
Client:   QUIT

docs.title: Receiving files (RECV)
docs.text:
The client requests RECV <name>. If the file exists and the destination allows download (according to upload_only), the server replies RECV SIZE <n>; the client, already knowing the size, can reject the download without further ado (it simply does not continue the session with the expected command). If the client confirms with RECV OK, the server sends the data block.

Client:   RECV <report.xml>
Server:   RECV SIZE 1024
Client:   RECV OK
Server:   <1024 bytes of data>

docs.title: Compression (ZSEND/ZRECV)
docs.text: ZSEND and ZRECV are the compressed variants of SEND/RECV: the data block is a ZIP file with a single entry (Deflate) instead of the clear content. They are enabled with the client's -z option; the rest of the command sequence is identical.

docs.title: Insecure mode operations (LS, MV)
docs.text: LS (listing the files that match a filter) and MV (downloading a file and then deleting it from the server) work only if the server started with the -I/insecure option. If insecure mode is off (the default value), the server logs the attempt and closes the connection without replying to the command.

docs.title: Password authentication (PASS)
docs.text: When the server requires a password, PASS must be the first command of the session. The client sends, in hexadecimal, the MD5 of the binary MD5 digest of the password (a double MD5). This obfuscates the password, it does not protect it: over a connection without TLS it adds no real security against someone who captures the traffic. For password authentication to contribute anything, it has to run over an encrypted connection.

docs.title: Encryption
docs.text: TLS wraps the whole connection from the first byte: there is no unencrypted phase and no later STARTTLS. Both ends must have TLS active; it is not negotiable mid-session.

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text: On any anomaly (an unknown command, a wrong password, more data than announced, an internal failure), the server closes the connection without explaining the reason to the client. The detail only remains in the server log, if it is active.

docs.title: File names and block size
docs.text: File names do not allow the characters ? [ ] / \ = + < > : ; ' , * ~ or any path (only the plain name). The block size for network reads and writes is 1024 bytes.

docs.title: The two Tentacle proxies
docs.text:
They should not be confused:

  • The Tentacle server in proxy mode (-b/-g or proxy_ip/proxy_port on the server): it forwards the whole connection to another Tentacle server, without storing anything. It is explained in section 3, "Proxy mode".
  • The client's HTTP proxy (-y user:password@address:port): the Tentacle client opens the connection through an HTTP proxy with CONNECT, with optional Basic authentication if a user and password are given. It is explained in section 2, "HTTP proxy".

docs.title: 2. The Tentacle client
docs.text: Syntax: tentacle_client [options] [file] [file] .... At least one file is needed, except in receive mode (-g), where the argument is the remote name to download.

docs.title: Command-line options
docs.text:
Same letters in both implementations:

Option Argument What it does Default -a address Server address. 127.0.0.1 -b local address Local address to bind the outgoing connection to. unset (chosen by the system) -c — Enables TLS without a client certificate. Incompatible with -e. off -e certificate OpenSSL certificate file of the client; enables TLS. Incompatible with -c. — -f CA Verifies that the server certificate is signed by this CA. Requires -e. — -g — Receive mode: downloads files from the server instead of sending them. off (send mode) -h — Shows the help. — -k key OpenSSL private key file of the client. Requires -e. — -p port Server port. 41121 -q — Quiet mode: does not print error messages. off -r number Retries of the network operations. Minimum 1: a lower value makes the client exit with a startup error. 3 -t seconds Timeout of the network operations. Minimum 1: a lower value makes the client exit with a startup error. 1 s -v — Verbose mode (logs the protocol events). off -w — Interactively asks for the private key password. It has effect only together with -e. off -x password Server password (PASS authentication). empty -y user:password@address:port HTTP proxy for the connection (CONNECT, with Basic if credentials are given). no proxy -z — Compresses the data in transit (ZSEND/ZRECV). off

docs.title: Combination rules
docs.text:
• -c and -e are incompatible with each other (two different ways of enabling TLS: without a certificate of its own or with one).
  • -f and -k require -e to be present; without a client certificate it makes no sense to ask for a CA or a key. -w has effect only together with -e.
  • IPv6: supported; the Perl client also needs the IO::Socket::INET6 module installed.

docs.title: HTTP proxy
docs.text: -y user:password@address:port makes the client open the connection to the proxy with a CONNECT to the real Tentacle server; if a user and password are given, it adds the Proxy-Authorization: Basic header. User and password are optional within the string.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: 0 if all the transfers on the command line ended well, 1 if any failed or if there was an error.

docs.title: Use from the EndPoint and the satellite server
docs.text: The EndPoint and the satellite server invoke the Tentacle client through four tokens of their configuration file: transfer_mode tentacle (the transfer mode), server_ip and server_port (destination) and server_opts (the client options of this section, as they are, for example server_opts -v -r 5). For the full detail of these tokens and their secondary server equivalents, see 9.1 · Full EndPoint configuration reference.

docs.title: Usage examples
docs.text:
With the server on 192.168.1.1 and no password on the client private key:

Simple transfer, with a maximum file size of 1 MB on the server:

tentacle_server -m 1048576 -s /tmp -v
tentacle_client -a 192.168.1.1 -v /home/user/myfile.dat

With password authentication:

tentacle_server -x password -s /tmp -v
tentacle_client -a 192.168.1.1 -x password -v /home/user/myfile.dat

TLS without a client certificate:

tentacle_server -e cert.pem -k key.pem -w -s /tmp -v
tentacle_client -a 192.168.1.1 -c -v /home/user/myfile.dat

TLS with a client certificate and password:

tentacle_server -x password -e cert.pem -k key.pem -f cacert.pem -w -s /tmp -v
tentacle_client \
  -a 192.168.1.1 \
  -x password \
  -e cert.pem \
  -k key.pem \
  -v /home/user/myfile.dat

docs.title: 3. The Tentacle server
docs.text: Syntax: tentacle_server -s <directory> [options], or tentacle_server -F <file> to start by reading the configuration from a file.

docs.title: Command-line options
docs.text: Option Token What it does Default -a addresses IPv4 addresses to listen on, separated by commas. 0.0.0.0 -b proxy_ip Proxy mode: address of the unreachable Tentacle server to forward to. — -c max_connections Maximum number of simultaneous connections. 10 -d daemon Runs the server as a daemon. Not available on Windows (see "Windows", further down). off -e ssl_cert OpenSSL certificate of the server; enables TLS. — -f ssl_ca CA with which to verify the client certificate. — -F — Full path to the configuration file. — -g proxy_port Proxy mode: port of the unreachable Tentacle server. 41121 -h — Shows the help. — -I insecure Enables insecure mode (LS and MV). off -i filters Distribution filters by subdirectory (regexp:dir;regexp:dir…). — -k ssl_key OpenSSL private key of the server. — -l log_file File to write the log to. standard output if not given -m max_size Maximum file size, in bytes. 64000000 -o overwrite Allows overwriting an existing file with the same name. off -p port Port to listen on. 41121 -q quiet Does not print error messages. off -r retries Retries of the network operations. Minimum 1. 3 -s directory Storage directory. Mandatory except in proxy mode. — -S — Manages the Windows service (install|uninstall|run). — -t timeout Timeout of the network operations, in seconds. Minimum 1. 1 -u ssl_cipher Restricts the admitted TLS 1.2 cipher suites, with OpenSSL names separated by :. normal negotiation -v verbose 1 Verbose mode: logs errors. off -V verbose 2 Extended verbose mode: logs errors and informational warnings. off -w — Asks for the private key password on the command line. It applies to encrypted PEM keys in the traditional format. off -x password Server password (PASS authentication). empty -z ssl_version Restricts the admitted TLS version to TLSv1_2 or TLSv1_3. normal negotiation (TLS 1.2 minimum)

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
The format is the usual one in the product: one line per token with the value after a space, and # comments out the whole line. The usual path of the file is /etc/tentacle/tentacle_server.conf. The command line takes precedence over the file when the same option is repeated in both places. There is no hot reload: a change in the file requires restarting the service.

Several tokens have no equivalent command-line option:

  • block_size: block size for network reads and writes, in bytes (1024 bytes by default; see "Protocol", further up).
  • download_only and upload_only: directories, after applying filters, from which only downloading or only uploading is allowed, respectively, separated by ;. They are detailed in "Filters and directories", further down.

docs.title: Package template versus internal values
docs.text: The template installed by the package (tentacle_server.conf.new) does not always match the default value applied by the binary itself when the token does not appear in the file. For example, the template enables daemon 1 even though the internal default value is 0 (off). The rest of the tokens in the previous table indicate, in the "Default" column, the internal value of the binary, not the one of the template.

docs.title: Filters and directories
docs.text: filters (-i) distributes the incoming files by subdirectory according to a regular expression on the name; the syntax is regexp:subdirectory;regexp:subdirectory;…. A file whose name does not match any filter is saved directly in the storage directory. The template of the main server distributes, among others, the .conf to conf, the .md5 to md5, the .zip to collections, the .lock to trans, the .rcmd to commands and the EndPoint installation packages (.agent_setup.exe, .agent_setup.tar.gz) to agent. download_only (-D) and upload_only (-U) act on these same subdirectories (already filtered), restricting what can be uploaded or downloaded in each one. After updating the package the server must be restarted so that it takes the new filters that the version brings.

docs.title: systemd service
docs.text: The main service is tentacle_serverd.service, with user pandora, which starts tentacle_server -F /etc/tentacle/tentacle_server.conf with a cleanup ExecStartPre (clean_tentacle_serverd, which empties the temporary files of the TMPDIR set in tentacle_server.env) and two environment files (tentacle_server.env with TMPDIR and tentacle_server_extra.env, the latter free for local adjustments). The relationship between this service and the tentacle_service_cmd / tentacle_service_watchdog tokens of the main server is in 9.3 · Remote configuration, Tentacle and synchronization.

docs.title: RMM instance
docs.text: RMM uses its own Tentacle instance, independent of the one of the main server: service tentacle_rmm.service (user root, port 41123, ExecStartPre with clean_tentacle_rmm), its own configuration file, its own storage directory (/var/spool/pandora/rmm_server) and its own TLS certificates. The filters (filters) distribute the RMM files by extension into their own subdirectories (rmm, res, queue, keepalive, data), and download_only/upload_only restrict those same subdirectories: downloading is only allowed from rmm, res and queue, and uploading is only allowed to data and keepalive. The template brings a sample password: it must be changed before putting the service into production, and like any secret, it is referenced from the configuration, never copied into the documentation or into a repository.

docs.title: Proxy mode
docs.text:
With -b/proxy_ip and -g/proxy_port, the Tentacle server does not act as a store: it forwards in raw form, byte by byte, everything that arrives from each client towards another Tentacle server (the "unreachable" one from the point of view of the clients). It can terminate TLS and password authentication in the client-proxy segment, with a different (or unencrypted) proxy-server segment. The satellite server solves the same forwarding with its own tokens, proxy_tentacle_from/proxy_tentacle_to; see 6.2 · Satellite servers.

Practical case: EndPoints behind a Tentacle proxy with TLS and password, end to end. First each segment is checked by hand and, if it works, the permanent configuration is set.

Manual tests:

# 1. Real server
sudo -u pandora tentacle_server \
  -x password \
  -e tentacle_cert \
  -k tentacle_key \
  -f ca_cert -s /tmp -v

# 2. Proxy
sudo -u pandora tentacle_server -b ip_server -g 41124

# 3. Client, against the proxy
sudo -u pandora tentacle_client \
  -a ip_proxy \
  -x password \
  -e tentacle_client_cert \
  -k tentacle_client_key \
  -v file

Permanent configuration, once the manual sending has been checked:

  1. Real server (/etc/tentacle/tentacle_server.conf):
password password
ssl_cert tentacle_cert
ssl_key tentacle_key
ssl_ca ca_cert
  1. Proxy (its own /etc/tentacle/tentacle_server.conf):
proxy_ip ip_server
proxy_port 41124
  1. EndPoint (pandora_agent.conf), pointing server_ip to the proxy, not to the real server:
server_opts -x password -e tentacle_client_cert -k tentacle_client_key
server_ip ip_proxy

Each option in server_opts is independent: if, for example, the password is not needed, it is enough to omit -x password from the line.

docs.title: Security: password, TLS and certificate combinations
docs.text:
The password (-x/password) and TLS are orthogonal: they can be combined or used separately. The four possible certificate combinations are the following; all of them allow adding a password in the same way.

1. Server with certificate, client without verification (the client does not check the identity of the server):

Manual test:

tentacle_server -v -e tentacle_cert -k tentacle_key -s /tmp
tentacle_client -v -c -a <server> file

Permanent configuration, server:

ssl_cert tentacle_cert
ssl_key tentacle_key

Permanent configuration, EndPoint and satellite server:

server_opts -c

2. Server with certificate, client verifies against a CA:

Manual test:

tentacle_server -v -e tentacle_cert -k tentacle_key -s /tmp
tentacle_client -v -e tentacle_client_cert -f ca_cert -a <server> file

Permanent configuration, server:

ssl_cert tentacle_cert
ssl_key tentacle_key

Permanent configuration, EndPoint and satellite server:

server_opts -e tentacle_client_cert -f ca_cert

3. Server verifies the client against a CA (client certificate without a CA of its own on the client):

Manual test:

tentacle_server -v -e tentacle_cert -k tentacle_key -f ca_cert -s /tmp
tentacle_client -v \
  -e tentacle_client_cert \
  -k tentacle_client_key \
  -a <server> file

Permanent configuration, server:

ssl_cert tentacle_cert
ssl_ca ca_cert
ssl_key tentacle_key

Permanent configuration, EndPoint and satellite server:

server_opts -e tentacle_client_cert -k tentacle_client_key

4. Mutual verification (server and client verify the certificate of the other against a CA):

Manual test:

tentacle_server -v -e tentacle_cert -k tentacle_key -f ca_cert -s /tmp
tentacle_client -v \
  -e tentacle_client_cert \
  -k tentacle_client_key \
  -f ca_cert \
  -a <server> file

Permanent configuration, server:

ssl_cert tentacle_cert
ssl_ca ca_cert
ssl_key tentacle_key

Permanent configuration, EndPoint and satellite server:

server_opts -e tentacle_client_cert -k tentacle_client_key -f ca_cert

In all cases, the certificate and key paths must be absolute in the configuration files, and the IO::Socket::SSL package has to be installed to use TLS with the Perl implementation. TLS requires version 1.2 at minimum.

For production, the recommended combination is 4 (mutual verification), with a password optionally added: it is the only one of the four in which both ends check the identity of the other against a CA.

retries/timeout (-r/-t) are not only network parameters: by limiting the retries and the timeout of each connection, they also make a brute-force attack against the password harder. The server log (-l/log_file, with the detail given by -v/-V) is, in addition to diagnostics, the audit record of the connections.

docs.title: Quick OpenSSL certificate guide
docs.text:
To generate the certificates used by the previous examples.

Create your own CA:

mkdir demoCA demoCA/newcerts demoCA/private
openssl req -new -x509 -keyout cakey.pem -out cacert.pem
mv cakey.pem demoCA/private/
mv cacert.pem demoCA/

Certificate request and signing with that CA:

openssl req -new -keyout tentaclekey.pem -out tentaclereq.pem -days 360
cat tentaclereq.pem tentaclekey.pem > tentaclenew.pem
touch demoCA/index.txt
echo "01" >> demoCA/serial
openssl ca -out tentaclecert.pem -in tentaclenew.pem

Self-signed certificate, without a CA:

openssl req -new -x509 -keyout tentaclekey.pem -out tentaclecert.pem -days 360

RSA key without a password (it avoids having to enter it on the client side):

openssl genrsa -out tentaclekey.pem

Export a PEM certificate to DER (needed on some systems):

openssl x509 -outform der -in tentaclecert.pem -out tentaclecert.der

docs.title: Windows
docs.text: On Windows, the server is managed as a service with tentacle_server -S install|uninstall|run; the -d option (Unix daemon) is not available on this platform.

docs.title: Database encryption
docs.text: An unencrypted database is honest to the point of indiscretion: whoever gets a dump takes away, along with the monitoring data, every password Pandora FMS stores on behalf of third parties. Database encryption shuts that mouth: it encrypts at the source the fields that hold passwords and secrets, so that a mysqldump lost, stolen or badly filed gives nothing readable away.

docs.title: What it is and what it protects
docs.text:
It is an Enterprise feature. The algorithm is 128-bit Rijndael in ECB mode, the same as AES-256-ECB through OpenSSL in the Web console, with a 256-bit key derived from the MD5 of the encryption passphrase (encryption_passphrase) entered in the configuration. That passphrase is not stored anywhere in the database, neither it nor the key that comes out of it: it lives only in the configuration files of each node. If it is lost, there is no way back: the encrypted passwords remain unreadable forever. Once configured, encryption is transparent: the Web console and the server encrypt when saving and decrypt when reading, with nobody having to do anything else.

What it protects, grouped by functional area:

What is encrypted Detail Monitoring Passwords of plugin modules and SNMPv3 credentials of modules, network components and policies. Inventory Passwords of the Enterprise inventory modules. Custom fields Agent custom fields marked as password type. Console configuration Mail server (SMTP) password; LDAP/Active Directory administration password (primary and secondary server) and the option to save a local copy of that password; historical database password; console replication database password; API access password; update proxy password; Pandora RC access password; remote command Web console password; automatic access hash password between nodes; credentials of the remote authentication sources of the Pandora FMS and Babel Enterprise type. High availability Database replication password between High Availability nodes. Server export Password of the data export server to another remote Pandora FMS. Command Center Connection data of each registered node (passwords of its databases, of its API and of its console). Plugins Hidden plugin macros. Credential manager The data of the stored credentials (users, passwords, keys and other access data of each type), see Credential manager.

What it does NOT protect: the access password of the Web console users uses a separate mechanism, with a non-reversible hash, and does not depend on this feature. Neither do the passwords that the Satellite server stores in its configuration: they have their own key (credential_pass) and their own mechanism, independent of this chapter.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text: Requirement Detail Edition Pandora FMS Enterprise. Without it, encryption_passphrase has no effect and the passwords are stored unencrypted. Access Administrator access to the configuration files of the Web console (config.php) and of the server (pandora_server.conf) of each node and of the Command Center. Service stop The Pandora FMS server must be stopped on each node and on the Command Center while pandora_encrypt_db runs. Encryption passphrase The same string in config.php and in pandora_server.conf, and the same on all the nodes and on the Command Center.

docs.title: Enabling encryption
docs.text:
The steps are repeated on the Command Center and on each node, in this order:

  1. Stop the Pandora FMS server.
  2. Add the same encryption_passphrase in config.php (/var/www/html/pandora_console/include/config.php, with the line $config["encryption_passphrase"]="passphrase";) and in pandora_server.conf (encryption_passphrase passphrase); in the latter it is commented out by default.
  3. Run pandora_encrypt_db /etc/pandora/pandora_server.conf (the full syntax is in Reference for pandora_encrypt_db).
  4. Restart the server.

docs.title: Changing the encryption passphrase
docs.text:
If the encryption passphrase has been compromised, replacing it in the configuration files is not enough: you have to decrypt with the old passphrase and encrypt again with the new one.

  1. Decrypt with the current passphrase: pandora_encrypt_db -d /etc/pandora/pandora_server.conf.
  2. Change encryption_passphrase in config.php and in pandora_server.conf, on all the nodes and on the Command Center.
  3. Encrypt again: pandora_encrypt_db /etc/pandora/pandora_server.conf.

Neither of the two steps uses the -m option: it is a legacy option from the migration between old versions and is not part of this procedure; using it here leaves some fields encrypted twice, with the old passphrase and with the new one, and unusable. More detail in Reference for pandora_encrypt_db.

docs.title: Removing encryption
docs.text:
1. Stop the server on the Command Center and on each node.
  2. Decrypt: pandora_encrypt_db -d /etc/pandora/pandora_server.conf.
  3. Comment out encryption_passphrase in config.php and in pandora_server.conf, on all the nodes and on the Command Center. In config.php the line looks like this: # $config["encryption_passphrase"]="passphrase";; in pandora_server.conf, #encryption_passphrase passphrase.
  4. Restart the server.

Keeping encryption enabled is recommended. Removing it leaves in plain text everything listed in What it is and what it protects.

docs.title: Consequences and precautions
docs.text:
• Identical passphrase everywhere. A node or the Command Center with a passphrase different from the rest will not be able to read the fields encrypted with another passphrase. The failure is silent: no visible exception is raised, you simply get meaningless bytes where a password should be.
  • Passphrase lost, credentials lost. There is no way to recover a forgotten encryption passphrase or to decrypt without it. Keep a backup of config.php and pandora_server.conf, the files that contain it, separate from the database backup, not next to it.
  • Protection against double execution. The tool remembers whether it has already encrypted or decrypted the database and refuses to repeat the same operation twice in a row: you have to decrypt before encrypting again, and vice versa.
  • High availability. The réplica de Alta Disponibilidad works at database level: it copies the already encrypted fields as they are, without decrypting them or encrypting them again. It is the correct and expected behaviour; there is no need to run pandora_encrypt_db on the replica node.
  • Backups. A backup of the database includes the encrypted fields as they are, and that is how it should be. To restore it you also need the encryption passphrase, which lives in the configuration files: keep it safe and separate, but available on the day you have to restore. A backup without its passphrase is only good for what is not a password.

docs.title: Reference for pandora_encrypt_db
docs.text: Field Value Installed path /usr/bin/pandora_encrypt_db (server package; it is deleted when uninstalling it). Usage pandora_encrypt_db [-d] [-m] <path to pandora_server.conf> -d Decrypt instead of encrypt. -m Legacy option for the migration from version 749 to 750: when used, the tool leaves untouched the additional fields of the credential manager credentials, both when encrypting and when decrypting. It is not part of the normal encryption, decryption or passphrase change procedure; use it only if you know exactly why you need it, never to change the encryption passphrase. Prerequisite encryption_passphrase must exist in the indicated configuration file; if it is missing, the script ends with a warning that password encryption is disabled.
